lines.text: I had a case a few hours ago -- a patient growing a possible second face inside her abdominal cavity. This nurse showed up in his off-shift, asking if he can help out. I swear, he was giddy about the whole thing.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.72]I had a case a few hours ago -- [2.16-6.07]a patient growing a possible second face inside her abdominal cavity. [6.62-10.13]This nurse showed up in his off-shift, asking if he can help out. [11.05-13.82]I swear, he was giddy about the whole thing.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37495

lines.subtitle: You ask that like most people don't sign up willingly.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37498
lines.text: You suggested it, remember?
lines.subtitle: You suggested it, remember?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37499
lines.text: Now I'm second-guessing.
lines.subtitle: Now I'm second-guessing.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37500
lines.text: Why’d you join? Tell me it wasn’t bribery or extortion.
lines.subtitle: [0-1]Why’d you join? [1.31-4.12]Tell me it wasn’t bribery or extortion.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_37501

lines.subtitle: [0-2.23]Let me guess: my clearance isn't high enough? [2.75-5.09]Heard that about a hundred times today already.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37503

lines.subtitle: How can I do my job if everything's classified?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37504

lines.subtitle: Fair enough. I won’t push the topic.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_37505
lines.text: I just...
lines.subtitle: I just...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_37506
lines.text: I've made a lot of mistakes. I'm trying to make up for them.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.05]I've made a lot of mistakes. [2.95-4.23]I'm trying to make up for them.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37507

lines.text: Hey, Dylan, before you go -- I could use your help with a body. It’s upstairs.
lines.subtitle: Hey, Dylan, before you go -- I could use your help with a body. It’s upstairs.

lines.text: Until we know what killed our headless patient upstairs, anyone who was in contact with the deceased needs to be quarantined. But I'm still waiting on finding access codes and every containment team is too busy to help.

lines.text: If you’re sure no one else is going to turn up with an exploded head, I’ll trust you. I’ve got enough to worry about as it is.

lines.text: Hey, Faden, you didn’t do half bad out there.

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57653
lines.text: Hey, forget that bet. Okay? It’s off. I don’t need any more bad karma. We almost lost the Oldest House.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.6]Hey, forget that bet. [3.13-5.11]Okay? It’s off. [5.99-8.31]I don’t need any more bad karma. [9.44-11]We almost lost the Oldest House.

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57657

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERHIGGINS_57649

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57650

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERHIGGINS_57651

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57652

lines.subtitle: No deal.

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57647
lines.text: Hey, nice going with the CFD! Good thing everyone was saved and nobody got hurt. It’s almost like the Director’s here!
lines.subtitle: [0-2.99]Hey, nice going with the CFD! [3.43-8.35]Good thing everyone was saved and nobody got hurt. It’s almost like the Director’s here!

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57648
lines.text: Asshole.
lines.subtitle: Asshole.

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERHIGGINS_57639
lines.text: Care to make it interesting?

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57640
lines.text: Go on.
lines.subtitle: Go on.

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERHIGGINS_57641
lines.text: Bet you ten bucks the Hiss don’t kill us all.
lines.subtitle: Bet you ten bucks the Hiss don’t kill us all.

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57642
lines.text: That’s easy. How about a hundred?

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERHIGGINS_57643

lines.subtitle: Seven thousand dol--

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57644
lines.text: Now, hang on, hang on. Okay, twenty bucks.

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERHIGGINS_57645

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57646

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57631
lines.text: Those Black Rock stockpiles came in handy, huh.

lines.text: I’m surprised someone hadn’t looted them by now.

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57633
lines.text: Who would steal a bunch of rocks?
lines.subtitle: Who would steal a bunch of rocks?

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERHIGGINS_57634
lines.text: In this city? Just about anyone. You could make some nice jewelry out of it, sell them for a high price.

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57635

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57627

lines.subtitle: The Hiss are acting differently, too.

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57629
lines.text: Maybe because they’re loose in the city? More space to spread out?

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERHIGGINS_57630

lines.subtitle: Maybe. Who knows.

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERFROST_57624
lines.text: Hey, isn’t that the Director’s brother? Who let him out?

lines.speaker: LWCHECKPOINTRANGERHIGGINS_57625
lines.text: Shit.
lines.subtitle: Shit.

lines.speaker: LWUNWELLAGENTKLEIN_57671
lines.text: I don’t know what to do... I don’t... It’s all over, there’s no way out... I can’t do this.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58000
lines.text: Maybe he made it.

lines.subtitle: I sure hope so.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58004
lines.text: And that... thing in the sky. And now Boris.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58005
lines.text: You... heard something?
lines.subtitle: [0-2.39]You... heard something?

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58006

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58007
lines.text: Ah, man...
lines.subtitle: Ah, man...

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58008
lines.text: I’m gonna miss that guy.
lines.subtitle: I’m gonna miss that guy.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58009
lines.text: Hey, you doing okay?
lines.subtitle: Hey, you doing okay?

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58010
lines.text: Fine.
lines.subtitle: Fine.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58011
lines.text: Saw one of our guys just... walking in circles. Just kept walking. And walking...
lines.subtitle: [0-1.89]Saw one of our guys just... [2.62-3.71]walking in circles. [4.84-7.86]Just kept walking. And walking...

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58012
lines.text: Shit.
lines.subtitle: Shit.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58013
lines.text: But me? I’m fine.
lines.subtitle: But me? I’m fine.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58014
lines.text: Hey... how’re you feeling about Arish?
lines.subtitle: [0-3.64]Hey... how’re you feeling about Arish?

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58015
lines.text: I dunno, man. He had a lot of demons.
lines.subtitle: I dunno, man. He had a lot of demons.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58016
lines.text: Yeah...
lines.subtitle: Yeah...

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58017
lines.text: He always did right by us. But the Hiss, the lockdown... it really wore him thin.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.56]He always did right by us. [2.02-5.29]But the Hiss, the lockdown... it really wore him thin.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58018
lines.text: Made him into a damn tough sonuvabitch, too.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.19]Made him into a damn tough sonuvabitch, too.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58019
lines.text: Yeah.
lines.subtitle: Yeah.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58020
lines.text: Mmh.
lines.subtitle: Mmh.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58021
lines.text: Hell of a guy.

lines.text: Hell of a guy.

lines.text: Arish is gone.

lines.text: Arish is dead.
lines.subtitle: Arish is dead.

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCEGOLDSTEIN_58114
lines.text: I kinda can’t believe we managed to build all of this. I know the containment plan was set up years ago, just in case, but...
lines.subtitle: [0-3.33]I kinda can’t believe we managed to build all of this. [4.03-8.6]I know the containment plan was set up years ago, just in case, but...

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCELILJESTROM_58115
lines.text: I know! When those trucks started rolling out of the Oldest House, and they just kept on coming...
lines.subtitle: [0.62-8.64]I know! When those trucks started rolling out of the Oldest House, and they just kept on coming...

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCEGOLDSTEIN_58116
lines.text: And here we are. Whatever else happens, we did this.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.42]And here we are. [1.6-4.63]Whatever else happens, we did this.

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCELILJESTROM_58117
lines.text: Yeah. Feels pretty good.
lines.subtitle: Yeah. Feels pretty good.

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCELILJESTROM_58118
lines.text: I really wish the containment plan didn’t have us seal off the zones so completely. If only we could drive vehicles through...
lines.subtitle: [0.62-6.83]I really wish the containment plan didn’t have us seal off the zones so completely. [7.56-10.11]If only we could drive vehicles through...

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCEGOLDSTEIN_58119
lines.text: Yeah, I know. Everybody’s going through ammo and everything else so fast, keeping them supplied is a real pain in the ass.
lines.subtitle: [0.53-2.88]Yeah, I know. [3.58-6.54]Everybody’s going through ammo and everything else so fast, [7.25-10]keeping them supplied is a real pain in the ass.

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCELILJESTROM_58120
lines.text: There must be something we can do.
lines.subtitle: There must be something we can do.

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCEGOLDSTEIN_58121
lines.text: Honestly? Pretty sure all we can do is make do, same as everybody else.
lines.subtitle: Honestly? Pretty sure all we can do is make do, same as everybody else.

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCELILJESTROM_58122
lines.text: All I have to do is look up and suddenly these walls we built are a joke. Just a complete joke.
lines.subtitle: [0.61-4.93]All I have to do is look up and suddenly these walls we built are a joke. [5.69-7.11]Just a complete joke.

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCEGOLDSTEIN_58123
lines.text: I know how you feel... but you can’t think like that. The walls do make a difference. At least we’re not dealing with everything all at once.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.13]I know how you feel... but you can’t think like that. [4.77-6.74]The walls do make a difference. [7.08-9.99]At least we’re not dealing with everything all at once.

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCELILJESTROM_58124
lines.text: Shut up and do your job, you mean?
lines.subtitle: [0.98-2.98]Shut up and do your job, you mean?

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCELILJESTROM_58125
lines.text: No. I hear you. You’re right.
lines.subtitle: [0.66-4.97]No. I hear you. You’re right.

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCEGOLDSTEIN_58126
lines.text: Hey... can I tell you a secret?
lines.subtitle: [0-2.86]Hey... can I tell you a secret?

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCELILJESTROM_58127
lines.text: Sure?
lines.subtitle: Sure?

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCEGOLDSTEIN_58128
lines.text: I didn’t really think we’d make it. When that thing appeared in the sky, I was like, “oh, okay, we’re fucked”.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.85]I didn’t really think we’d make it. [2.62-9.47]When that thing appeared in the sky, I was like, “oh, okay, we’re fucked”.

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCELILJESTROM_58129
lines.text: Yeah. Me too. But..
lines.subtitle: [0.62-4.48]Yeah. Me too. But..

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCEGOLDSTEIN_58130
lines.text: Here we are.
lines.subtitle: Here we are.

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCELILJESTROM_58131
lines.text: Yeah.
lines.subtitle: Yeah.

lines.speaker: LWFOMAINTENANCELILJESTROM_58132
lines.text: Sooo... do you have any idea how we’re supposed to clean this mess up?
lines.subtitle: [0.57-5.38]Sooo... do you have any idea how we’re supposed to clean this mess up?

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTHEINEKEN_57945
lines.text: Never thought we’d be testing this stuff just out in the open like this.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.32]Never thought we’d be testing this stuff just out in the open like this.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBERGER_57946
lines.text: Yeah... we’re not exactly following OSHA regulations, are we?
lines.subtitle: [0.6-4.78]Yeah... we’re not exactly following OSHA regulations, are we?

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTHEINEKEN_57947
lines.text: I won’t tell ‘em if you won’t.
lines.subtitle: I won’t tell ‘em if you won’t.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBERGER_57948
lines.text: I kinda feel like we should...
lines.subtitle: I kinda feel like we should...

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBERGER_57949
lines.text: “Dear diary, today I helped turn a good chunk of Manhattan into a war zone by supplying Bureau-issued landmines, of all things...”
lines.subtitle: [0.54-8.36]“Dear diary, today I helped turn a good chunk of Manhattan into a war zone by supplying Bureau-issued landmines, of all things...”

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTHEINEKEN_57950
lines.text: Better than the alternative.
lines.subtitle: Better than the alternative.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBERGER_57951
lines.text: Yeah. Still, though...
lines.subtitle: Yeah. Still, though...

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTHEINEKEN_57952
lines.text: We’re running low on detonators.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.98]We’re running low on detonators.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBERGER_57953
lines.text: I’ll put in an order to the Oldest House.
lines.subtitle: I’ll put in an order to the Oldest House.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTHEINEKEN_57954
lines.text: Ask them to throw in a pizza while you’re at it.
lines.subtitle: Ask them to throw in a pizza while you’re at it.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBERGER_57955
lines.text: I didn’t know I was working with an optimist.
lines.subtitle: [0.53-2.54]I didn’t know I was working with an optimist.

lines.subtitle: [0-3.42]Crap. I lost my needle-nose pliers.

lines.subtitle: [0-2.9]I want my needle-nose pliers.

lines.text: What’s the difference?

lines.text: The handle is perfectly molded to my fingers.

lines.subtitle: Ohhh-kay.

lines.text: Dude...
lines.subtitle: Dude...

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBERGER_57965
lines.text: Just ignore him. He obviously wants attention.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.57]Just ignore him. [1.8-3.65]He obviously wants attention.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTTAMBOLI_57966

lines.subtitle: I have to say, I really dislike these balloons.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBALDERAS_57967
lines.text: Yeah, I know. I’d prefer drones myself. But these damn gravity fields, and, you know, the Bureau’s budget...
lines.subtitle: [0-3.26]Yeah, I know. I’d prefer drones myself. [3.36-6.99]But these damn gravity fields, and, you know, the Bureau’s budget...

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTTAMBOLI_57968

lines.subtitle: [0-1.19]Yes, of course. [1.72-4.43]I just wish we had more control over them.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBALDERAS_57969

lines.subtitle: [0-3.37]Hey, at least they’re a cheap and easy way to get a ton of sensors up there.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBALDERAS_57970
lines.text: Starting to get some pretty decent mapping data now...
lines.subtitle: Starting to get some pretty decent mapping data now...

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTTAMBOLI_57971
lines.text: How bad is it?
lines.subtitle: How bad is it?

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBALDERAS_57972
lines.text: Well... not great. Manhattan’s seriously messed up.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.56]Well... not great. [2.08-3.86]Manhattan’s seriously messed up.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTTAMBOLI_57973
lines.text: We’ll find a way to fix it.
lines.subtitle: We’ll find a way to fix it.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBALDERAS_57974
lines.text: Sure hope you’re right about that, brother. Things are feeling a little too apocalyptic for my taste.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.22]Sure hope you’re right about that, brother. [2.97-5.79]Things are feeling a little too apocalyptic for my taste.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBALDERAS_57975
lines.text: Hey! C’mon, man!
lines.subtitle: Hey! C’mon, man!

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTTAMBOLI_57976
lines.text: You don’t see us messing with your work, do you?
lines.subtitle: [0-3.18]You don’t see us messing with your work, do you?

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBALDERAS_57977
lines.text: This guy. What the hell.
lines.subtitle: This guy. What the hell.

lines.speaker: LWTASCIENTISTBALDERAS_57978
lines.text: Why would you do it again?

lines.text: I wish I had a best friend like Fred.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.79]I wish I had a best friend like Fred.

lines.subtitle: [0-1.54]That new Director... [2.41-5.95]really making the best out of an awful situation.

lines.text: So... what’s the next move? Any word from anybody in charge?

lines.subtitle: [0-1.62]He got a field promotion. [2.31-4.1]He’s now a Senior Asshole.

lines.speaker: LWAGENTREYES_57772
lines.text: Dick. I thought he was dead. You have the worst sense of humor.
lines.subtitle: [0.75-3.88]Dick. I thought he was dead. [4.09-5.92]You have the worst sense of humor.

lines.speaker: LWFIELDRESEARCHERJANUSZ_57773
lines.text: I don’t know what you’re talking about.
lines.subtitle: I don’t know what you’re talking about.

lines.speaker: LWAGENTREYES_57774
lines.text: Of course, making me laugh was how you bagged me all those years ago...
lines.subtitle: [1.18-4.4]Of course, making me laugh was how you bagged me all those years ago...

lines.speaker: LWFIELDRESEARCHERJANUSZ_57775
lines.text: Shh. All right, all right. There’s people here. I don’t wanna have to talk to HR about our--
lines.subtitle: [0-2.41]Shh. All right, all right. [2.8-3.81]There’s people here. [4.58-7.36]I don’t wanna have to talk to HR about our--

lines.speaker: LWAGENTREYES_57776
lines.text: What was that? Our relationship? You want me to be louder, honey?
lines.subtitle: [1.4-2.4]What was that? [2.67-5.89]Our relationship? You want me to be louder, honey?

lines.speaker: LWFIELDRESEARCHERJANUSZ_57777
lines.text: All right! Sheesh.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.91]All right! Sheesh.

lines.speaker: LWAGENTREYES_57778
lines.text: How’s things?
lines.subtitle: How’s things?

lines.speaker: LWFIELDRESEARCHERJANUSZ_57779
lines.text: Nothing much to report over here. Weirdly calm for a zone so badly Patterned.
lines.subtitle: [0.53-2.54]Nothing much to report over here. [3.7-6.3]Weirdly calm for a zone so badly Patterned.

lines.speaker: LWAGENTREYES_57780
lines.text: No news is good news.
lines.subtitle: [0.9-2.99]No news is good news.

lines.speaker: LWFIELDRESEARCHERJANUSZ_57781
lines.text: I’d rather have news like: “Congrats, the city is saved! Everything’s back to normal!”
lines.subtitle: [0.6-3.71]I’d rather have news like: “Congrats, the city is saved! [4.23-5.59]Everything’s back to normal!”

lines.speaker: LWAGENTREYES_57782
lines.text: You wouldn’t even know what to do with yourself without a crisis.
lines.subtitle: [0.62-3.53]You wouldn’t even know what to do with yourself without a crisis.

lines.speaker: LWFIELDRESEARCHERJANUSZ_57783
lines.text: How’s logistics looking?
lines.subtitle: How’s logistics looking?

lines.speaker: LWAGENTREYES_57784
lines.text: Logistical. A lot of moving pieces, a lot gear to haul. Had a nasty blow-out.
lines.subtitle: [0.65-5.2]Logistical. A lot of moving pieces, a lot gear to haul. [5.76-7.2]Had a nasty blow-out.

lines.speaker: LWFIELDRESEARCHERJANUSZ_57785
lines.text: With who?
lines.subtitle: With who?

lines.speaker: LWAGENTREYES_57786
lines.text: With a tire on my truck.
lines.subtitle: With a tire on my truck.

lines.speaker: LWFIELDRESEARCHERJANUSZ_57787
lines.text: Oh. I was steeling myself for drama.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.06]Oh. I was steeling myself for drama.

lines.speaker: LWAGENTREYES_57788
lines.text: Haha!
lines.subtitle: Haha!

lines.speaker: LWAGENTREYES_57789
lines.text: Seems like I’ve got some news for you: “Congrats, the city is saved!”
lines.subtitle: [0.82-4.93]Seems like I’ve got some news for you: “Congrats, the city is saved!”

lines.speaker: LWFIELDRESEARCHERJANUSZ_57790
lines.text: I don’t believe in manifestation, but this one worked out nicely. Not that we’re back to normal, exactly, but I’ll take it.
lines.subtitle: [0.53-4.19]I don’t believe in manifestation, but this one worked out nicely. [4.97-9.16]Not that we’re back to normal, exactly, but I’ll take it.

lines.speaker: LWAGENTREYES_57791
lines.text: Ask and you shall receive.
lines.subtitle: Ask and you shall receive.

lines.speaker: LWAGENTREYES_57792
lines.text: We should have lunch together at the Field Office when they let you leave that place.
lines.subtitle: We should have lunch together at the Field Office when they let you leave that place.

lines.speaker: LWFIELDRESEARCHERJANUSZ_57793
lines.text: Deal.
lines.subtitle: Deal.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57382
lines.text: I have a theory.
lines.subtitle: [0.56-2.64]I have a theory.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57383
lines.text: Yes?
lines.subtitle: Yes?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57384
lines.text: There seems to be a connection between some paranatural entities or items and resonances - in this particular case, musical resonances.
lines.subtitle: [0-5.27]There seems to be a connection between some paranatural entities or items and resonances - [5.37-8.04]in this particular case, musical resonances.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57385
lines.text: You mean the Karaoke Machine Altered Item might not only be using resonances to allow itself to operate, but that it might have been created by them? A symbiotic, or near ouroboric, relationship between the Item and its mode of operation?
lines.subtitle: [0-7.77]You mean the Karaoke Machine Altered Item might not only be using resonances to allow itself to operate, but that it might have been created by them? [8.75-14.13]A symbiotic, or near ouroboric, relationship between the Item and its mode of operation?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57386
lines.text: Uh, well, no, I... uh, I was thinking... something else. But this is better.
lines.subtitle: [0.63-3.73]Uh, well, no, I... uh, I was thinking... [4.66-7.92]something else. But this is better.

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTKONTOS_57714
lines.text: Isn’t that Faden?
lines.subtitle: Isn’t that Faden?

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTGREEN_57715
lines.text: Yep.
lines.subtitle: Yep.

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTGREEN_57716
lines.text: Hey, keep up the good work!
lines.subtitle: Hey, keep up the good work!

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTKONTOS_57717
lines.text: Don’t talk to him. You don’t know what he’ll... do.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.61]Don’t talk to him. [2.5-4.36]You don’t know what he’ll... do.

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTGREEN_57718
lines.text: Did you hear the Sinkhole was filled with civilians?
lines.subtitle: [0.52-2.7]Did you hear the Sinkhole was filled with civilians?

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTKONTOS_57719
lines.text: Yeah, Patterned to hell and back.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.07]Yeah, Patterned to hell and back.

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTGREEN_57720
lines.text: A grim way to go.
lines.subtitle: A grim way to go.

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTKONTOS_57721
lines.text: What’s a non-grim way to go?
lines.subtitle: [0.63-2.76]What’s a non-grim way to go?

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTGREEN_57722
lines.text: Falling asleep in a field of flowers, listening to bird song, the sun shining on your face.
lines.subtitle: Falling asleep in a field of flowers, listening to bird song, the sun shining on your face.

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTKONTOS_57723
lines.text: Wow, you just had that right in the chamber?
lines.subtitle: [0-3.06]Wow, you just had that right in the chamber?

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTGREEN_57724
lines.text: It just sounds nice, that’s all.
lines.subtitle: It just sounds nice, that’s all.

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTKONTOS_57725
lines.text: If I had to go, I’d like it to be something like... fixing up the old Mustang, having some people over for a barbecue, full stomach, enough drinks to get a little fuzzy, and then I’d just... nod off in the lawn chair and never wake up again.
lines.subtitle: [1.04-4.37]If I had to go, I’d like it to be something like... [4.8-9.84]fixing up the old Mustang, having some people over for a barbecue, full stomach, [10.06-13.89]enough drinks to get a little fuzzy, and then I’d just... [14.3-17.18]nod off in the lawn chair and never wake up again.

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTGREEN_57726
lines.text: Yeah. That sounds pretty good.
lines.subtitle: Yeah. That sounds pretty good.

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTKONTOS_57727
lines.text: Of course, in our line of work...
lines.subtitle: [1.01-3.44]Of course, in our line of work...

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTGREEN_57728
lines.text: “Wiped out by a paranatural entity slash force” does seem more likely right now, yeah.
lines.subtitle: “Wiped out by a paranatural entity slash force” does seem more likely right now, yeah.

lines.speaker: LWLAUNDROMATAGENTKONTOS_57729
lines.text: Yeeep.
lines.subtitle: Yeeep.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTCLAIR_58340
lines.text: You think Rach is gonna be okay?
lines.subtitle: You think Rach is gonna be okay?

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTMACHOWARD_58341
lines.text: That Mold hunger is no joke. But I think she can hold out.
lines.subtitle: [1.02-3.11]That Mold hunger is no joke. [4.35-6.67]But I think she can hold out.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTCLAIR_58342
lines.text: Sure wish we had a working antidote right about now...
lines.subtitle: [0-2.99]Sure wish we had a working antidote right about now...

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTMACHOWARD_58343
lines.text: New strains of Mold. What can you do?
lines.subtitle: [1.15-2.56]New strains of Mold. [3.3-4.9]What can you do?

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTMACHOWARD_58344
lines.text: I can’t believe the Mold grew this much this quickly. It wasn’t like this inside the Oldest House.
lines.subtitle: [0.71-3.33]I can’t believe the Mold grew this much this quickly. [4.79-6.86]It wasn’t like this inside the Oldest House.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTCLAIR_58345
lines.text: I have a theory that the House itself impeded its growth somehow.
lines.subtitle: [0.55-5.64]I have a theory that the House itself impeded its growth somehow.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTMACHOWARD_58346
lines.text: What’s that based on?
lines.subtitle: What’s that based on?

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTCLAIR_58347
lines.text: Oh, that’s based on the Oldest House being really damn weird. And the Mold being a lot worse out here.
lines.subtitle: [0.52-4.42]Oh, that’s based on the Oldest House being really damn weird. [4.63-7.23]And the Mold being a lot worse out here.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTMACHOWARD_58348
lines.text: Heh.
lines.subtitle: Heh.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTMACHOWARD_58349
lines.text: It’s kinda beautiful, though. Smells good, too.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.7]It’s kinda beautiful, though. [3.48-4.81]Smells good, too.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTCLAIR_58350
lines.text: Hey, watch it.
lines.subtitle: Hey, watch it.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTCLAIR_58351
lines.text: So, even if we deal with this Hedron threat and the Hiss. Say we just... take ‘em both out, problem solved.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.51]So, even if we deal with this Hedron threat and the Hiss. [5.15-8.11]Say we just... take ‘em both out, problem solved.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTMACHOWARD_58352
lines.text: I like this so far. But I see where you’re going.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.82]I like this so far. [2.28-4.4]But I see where you’re going.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTCLAIR_58353
lines.text: Yeah, what about the Mold? At least we had it contained in the Oldest House. Now it’s outside. It could be in the water.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.98]Yeah, what about the Mold? [2.81-4.74]At least we had it contained in the Oldest House. [4.74-6.96]Now it’s outside. It could be in the water.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTMACHOWARD_58354
lines.text: I know. It scares the crap out of me.
lines.subtitle: I know. It scares the crap out of me.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTCLAIR_58355
lines.text: Hey, uh... you felt any of those Patterning symptoms?
lines.subtitle: Hey, uh... you felt any of those Patterning symptoms?

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTMACHOWARD_58356
lines.text: No. You?
lines.subtitle: No. You?

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTCLAIR_58357
lines.text: No... Well, I’ve had some thoughts that keep going around in my head. Like, a lot. A lot a lot.
lines.subtitle: [0.58-5.46]No... Well, I’ve had some thoughts that keep going around in my head. [5.61-6.61]Like, a lot. [7.13-8.31]A lot a lot.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTMACHOWARD_58358
lines.text: So you’re playing the exciting game of “anxiety or paranatural influence.”
lines.subtitle: So you’re playing the exciting game of “anxiety or paranatural influence.”

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTCLAIR_58359
lines.text: Kind of banking on the former.
lines.subtitle: Kind of banking on the former.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTMACHOWARD_58360
lines.text: I got your back, either way.
lines.subtitle: I got your back, either way.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTMACHOWARD_58361
lines.text: So, this thing with Underhill... You think she really lost her mind?
lines.subtitle: [0-3.53]So, this thing with Underhill... [5.55-7.35]You think she really lost her mind?

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTCLAIR_58362
lines.text: No. She’s not the type. I bet she just decided to be even more difficult than normal. She just took her shit and went home.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.09]No. She’s not the type. [3.09-8.14]I bet she just decided to be even more difficult than normal. She just took her shit and went home.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTMACHOWARD_58363
lines.text: That tracks. Still could use her expertise, though...
lines.subtitle: [1.83-6.52]That tracks. Still could use her expertise, though...

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTCLAIR_58364
lines.text: Yeah, I mean, I hate her so much but I’d pay good money to have her back here, telling us how that gunk works. Being annoyed. Condescending... I think I miss her.
lines.subtitle: [0-6.92]Yeah, I mean, I hate her so much but I’d pay good money to have her back here, [7.45-9.49]telling us how that gunk works. [9.74-14.57]Being annoyed. Condescending... I think I miss her.

lines.speaker: LWMBRADIOSCIENTISTARONTHAL_58365
lines.text: Just keep breathing, okay? Try to meditate or something.
lines.subtitle: [0.71-3.4]Just keep breathing, okay? [3.92-5.67]Try to meditate or something.

lines.speaker: LWMBRADIOSCIENTISTREYES-SMITH_58366
lines.text: That’s pointless. That’s not gonna do anything.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.76]That’s pointless. That’s not gonna do anything.

lines.speaker: LWMBRADIOSCIENTISTARONTHAL_58367
lines.text: It feels that way. But once you get over the hump, it starts to get easier.
lines.subtitle: [0.77-1.78]It feels that way. [1.88-5.51]But once you get over the hump, it starts to get easier.

lines.speaker: LWMBRADIOSCIENTISTREYES-SMITH_58368
lines.text: It’s not getting easier! What do you know?
lines.subtitle: [0.67-1.92]It’s not getting easier! [2.41-3.48]What do you know?

lines.speaker: LWMBRADIOSCIENTISTARONTHAL_58369
lines.text: Oh yeah, ‘cause I’ve never been through that, right?
lines.subtitle: [0.6-3.69]Oh yeah, ‘cause I’ve never been through that, right?

lines.speaker: LWMBRADIOSCIENTISTREYES-SMITH_58370
lines.text: Sorry. I know. I’m sorry. I just -- I’m so hungry. I ate lunch but it just... tastes like nothing now.
lines.subtitle: [0.56-2.04]Sorry. I know. [2.94-6.17]I’m sorry. I just -- I’m so hungry. [7.21-8.51]I ate lunch but it just... [9.5-10.72]tastes like nothing now.

lines.speaker: LWMBRADIOSCIENTISTARONTHAL_58371
lines.text: Stop thinking about it. Just keep breathing.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.75]Stop thinking about it. [1.85-4.35]Just keep breathing.

lines.speaker: LWMBRADIOSCIENTISTARONTHAL_58372
lines.text: Just keep breathing.
lines.subtitle: [0.61-3.67]Just keep breathing.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTROBBS_58373
lines.text: I’m okay. I’m okay. I just... feel like I gotta go somewhere. I don’t know where.
lines.subtitle: [1.08-2.83]I’m okay. I’m okay. [3.13-6.29]I just... feel like I gotta go somewhere. [6.74-8.16]I don’t know where.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTBRICKSTONE_58374
lines.text: You’re doing okay. Are you having any other strange feelings?
lines.subtitle: [0-1.44]You’re doing okay. [1.93-4.23]Are you having any other strange feelings?

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTROBBS_58375
lines.text: Feels like a bit of a loaded question, given where we are.
lines.subtitle: [0.67-6.15]Feels like a bit of a loaded question, given where we are.

lines.speaker: LWMBRANGERSEEGER_58376
lines.text: Maybe try to answer it anyway.
lines.subtitle: Maybe try to answer it anyway.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTBRICKSTONE_58377
lines.text: Hey, I got this, thanks.
lines.subtitle: Hey, I got this, thanks.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTROBBS_58378
lines.text: I just... gotta get moving...
lines.subtitle: I just... gotta get moving...

lines.speaker: LWMBRANGERSEEGER_58379
lines.text: So, uh... your friend who was feeling weird... you, uh... think he ended up as a part of that Mold Resonant thing?
lines.subtitle: [0-3.96]So, uh... your friend who was feeling weird... [4.06-8.78]you, uh... think he ended up as a part of that Mold Resonant thing?

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTBRICKSTONE_58380
lines.text: Fuck. I don’t know. It could’ve been anything.
lines.subtitle: [0.87-6]Fuck. I don’t know. It could’ve been anything.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTBRICKSTONE_58381
lines.text: I mean, he probably did.
lines.subtitle: [1.14-4.72]I mean, he probably did.

lines.speaker: LWMBRANGERSEEGER_58382
lines.text: I’m sorry.
lines.subtitle: I’m sorry.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTBRICKSTONE_58383
lines.text: Me too.
lines.subtitle: Me too.

lines.speaker: LWMBRANGERSEEGER_58384
lines.text: Hey, I heard a lot of stories about this Dr. Underhill...
lines.subtitle: [0.62-4.22]Hey, I heard a lot of stories about this Dr. Underhill...

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTBRICKSTONE_58385
lines.text: Oh, you have no idea. You weren’t with us during the lockdown. She was incredibly difficult. Almost as much as when she was here.
lines.subtitle: [0.78-5.03]Oh, you have no idea. You weren’t with us during the lockdown. [5.65-7.96]She was incredibly difficult. [8.46-10.38]Almost as much as when she was here.

lines.speaker: LWMBRANGERSEEGER_58386
lines.text: I heard she tried to go head to head with Acting Director Pope or something before she disappeared?
lines.subtitle: [0.56-5.59]I heard she tried to go head to head with Acting Director Pope or something before she disappeared?

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTBRICKSTONE_58387
lines.text: It’s possible. It certainly wouldn’t be out of character.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.62]It’s possible. It certainly wouldn’t be out of character.

lines.speaker: LWMBRANGERSEEGER_58388
lines.text: I bet the Bureau’s got her locked her up somewhere. You can’t buck the system.
lines.subtitle: [0.79-4.97]I bet the Bureau’s got her locked her up somewhere. You can’t buck the system.

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTBRICKSTONE_58389
lines.text: Those Mold clones are something else. A very cool new thing.
lines.subtitle: [0.64-2.75]Those Mold clones are something else. [2.85-4.44]A very cool new thing.

lines.speaker: LWMBRANGERSEEGER_58390
lines.text: Cool? Really? I’d go with “creepy abominations.”
lines.subtitle: [0.63-5.25]Cool? Really? I’d go with “creepy abominations.”

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTBRICKSTONE_58391
lines.text: I guess both can be true. Anyway, we’re learning a lot.
lines.subtitle: [0.67-1.98]I guess both can be true. [2.52-4.06]Anyway, we’re learning a lot.

lines.speaker: LWMBRANGERSEEGER_58392
lines.text: I don’t like these Mold clones, but I guess they’re kind of harmless?
lines.subtitle: [0.63-4.41]I don’t like these Mold clones, but I guess they’re kind of harmless?

lines.speaker: LWMBSCIENTISTBRICKSTONE_58393
lines.text: They don’t behave at all like the rest of the Mold. But I think sooner or later, we’ll have to, you know, do something about them. Seems like a shame.
lines.subtitle: [0.66-2.74]They don’t behave at all like the rest of the Mold. [3.65-8.14]But I think sooner or later, we’ll have to, you know, do something about them. [9.94-10.94]Seems like a shame.

lines.speaker: LWMBRANGERSEEGER_58394
lines.text: I’m not gonna lose any sleep over it.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.83]I’m not gonna lose any sleep over it.

lines.speaker: LWADMINRAY_57524
lines.text: We need more Rangers at checkpoints. We can’t have workers getting killed because the guard was on a lunch break!
lines.subtitle: [0-2.06]We need more Rangers at checkpoints. [2.47-6.28]We can’t have workers getting killed because the guard was on a lunch break!

lines.speaker: LWADMINCAMPOS_57525
lines.text: Lunch breaks are guaranteed by the regs.
lines.subtitle: [0.6-2.84]Lunch breaks are guaranteed by the regs.

lines.speaker: LWADMINRAY_57526
lines.text: Are you trying to piss me off, Campos?
lines.subtitle: [0-2.65]Are you trying to piss me off, Campos?

lines.speaker: LWADMINQUINN_57527
lines.text: Let’s not get excited. Or distracted. We’ll allocate more Rangers to guard duty.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.1]Let’s not get excited. [2.25-5.67]Or distracted. We’ll allocate more Rangers to guard duty.

lines.speaker: LWADMINRAY_57528
lines.text: Damn fucking straight.
lines.subtitle: Damn fucking straight.

lines.speaker: LWADMINQUINN_57529
lines.text: The Black Rock supply is a concern.
lines.subtitle: The Black Rock supply is a concern.

lines.speaker: LWADMINCAMPOS_57530
lines.text: I’d get the Research Department on it - let’s see if they can find a way to make what we have last longer. Squeeze water from a stone.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.06]I’d get the Research Department on it - [2.32-5.21]let’s see if they can find a way to make what we have last longer. [5.44-6.92]Squeeze water from a stone.

lines.speaker: LWADMINQUINN_57531
lines.text: I wish we weren’t so dependent on injector fluid.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.38]I wish we weren’t so dependent on injector fluid.

lines.speaker: LWADMINRAY_57532
lines.text: I wish it didn’t make my kidneys hurt and my shit like lava. But I guess it beats the alternative.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.65]I wish it didn’t make my kidneys hurt and my shit like lava. [4.6-7.16]But I guess it beats the alternative.

lines.speaker: LWADMINRAY_57533
lines.text: We’re gonna have to dig out more gear for Research at some point. The Mold’s getting everywhere, it seems like.
lines.subtitle: [0-5.01]We’re gonna have to dig out more gear for Research at some point. [5.53-8.09]The Mold’s getting everywhere, it seems like.

lines.speaker: LWADMINCAMPOS_57534
lines.text: So, what, suits and sampling gear?
lines.subtitle: [0.74-4.49]So, what, suits and sampling gear?

lines.speaker: LWADMINRAY_57535
lines.text: Especially suits. Might need to dig into the storage, see if we can find some musty old shit that’s not already been handed out.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.27]Especially suits. Might need to dig into the storage, [4.77-8.72]see if we can find some musty old shit that’s not already been handed out.

lines.speaker: LWADMINQUINN_57536
lines.text: Good luck with that. I mean, genuinely.
lines.subtitle: [0.61-2.14]Good luck with that. [3.3-5.48]I mean, genuinely.

lines.speaker: LWADMINCAMPOS_57537

lines.text: What can we learn from the failed attempt at evacuating Manhattan?
lines.subtitle: [0.62-3.96]What can we learn from the failed attempt at evacuating Manhattan?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57306

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57307
lines.text: Besides that. I believe there were very early signs of the approaching AWE, weeks in advance of when they were first noticed. Had we identified them sooner, we might have succeeded.
lines.subtitle: [0.81-5.69]Besides that. I believe there were very early signs of the approaching AWE, [5.79-8.01]weeks in advance of when they were first noticed. [8.54-11.79]Had we identified them sooner, we might have succeeded.

lines.text: Hmm.
lines.subtitle: Hmm.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57311
lines.text: What I’m interested in is the Pattern Barrier. There are pros and cons to this quote unquote force field.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57313

lines.subtitle: [0.57-4.24]Another pro: the Patterning likely affects only the inside. [4.95-11.56]Con: it might be amplified by its spatial restrictions -- reverberating, multiplying exponentially.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57314

lines.subtitle: [0-2.23]What are the long-term implications? [2.89-6.44]An increasingly Patterning city, folding in on itself?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57315

lines.subtitle: [0-1.22]A second Resonant Entity! [1.42-3.65]Exciting. More data for us to dissect, so to speak. [4.32-7.26]Not that these are lab rats for us to cut into, of course.

lines.subtitle: [0.9-9.21]Well, the first one certainly, uhm... gave us a lot to delve into.

lines.subtitle: [0.77-4.98]Hey, you think that Threshold that chopped off all those heads is still a threat?

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERGARCIA_57465
lines.text: “Chopped”? Not how I heard it described. They say the entity is dealt with. Doesn’t mean there can’t be more of ‘em out there, though.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.97]“Chopped”? Not how I heard it described. They say the entity is dealt with. [5.44-7.73]Doesn’t mean there can’t be more of ‘em out there, though.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERPHAM_57466
lines.text: Yeah, we can never really be sure, can we?
lines.subtitle: Yeah, we can never really be sure, can we?

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERGARCIA_57467
lines.text: I guess any more bodies with missing heads will be the tip-off.
lines.subtitle: I guess any more bodies with missing heads will be the tip-off.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERGARCIA_57468
lines.text: If you ask me, if we wanna make sure no more people lose their heads, we should blow up the whole Threshold site.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.07]If you ask me, if we wanna make sure no more people lose their heads, [4.17-6.21]we should blow up the whole Threshold site.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERPHAM_57469
lines.text: Is that your answer to everything, explosives?
lines.subtitle: [0.58-3.64]Is that your answer to everything, explosives?

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERGARCIA_57470
lines.text: I can’t name a time explosives didn’t work out great.
lines.subtitle: I can’t name a time explosives didn’t work out great.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERGARCIA_57471
lines.text: Well... there was that landslide in Colorado. But that one wasn’t on me.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.08]Well... there was that landslide in Colorado. [3.72-4.72]But that one wasn’t on me.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERPHAM_57472
lines.text: What do you think of the prepper? He finally got what he’d been waiting for all these years.
lines.subtitle: [0.54-1.76]What do you think of the prepper? [2.4-4.86]He finally got what he’d been waiting for all these years.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERGARCIA_57473
lines.text: Nothing wrong with survivalism. I do take offense to the guy stealing our gear, though.
lines.subtitle: Nothing wrong with survivalism. I do take offense to the guy stealing our gear, though.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERPHAM_57474
lines.text: Yeah, we gotta beef up the security on our warehouses. Somebody just walks away with our land mines and blows up our people?
lines.subtitle: [0-3.18]Yeah, we gotta beef up the security on our warehouses. [3.84-7.58]Somebody just walks away with our land mines and blows up our people?

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERGARCIA_57475
lines.text: Fucking embarrassing.
lines.subtitle: Fucking embarrassing.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERPHAM_57476
lines.text: I’ve been thinking more about that survivalist... If you take out the fanaticism angle... huh.
lines.subtitle: [0.58-2.91]I’ve been thinking more about that survivalist... [3.56-7.25]If you take out the fanaticism angle... huh.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERGARCIA_57477
lines.text: Being ready means you don’t gotta get ready.
lines.subtitle: Being ready means you don’t gotta get ready.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERPHAM_57478
lines.text: Wish we’d been ready for this AWE.
lines.subtitle: [0.65-2.97]Wish we’d been ready for this AWE.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERGARCIA_57479
lines.text: This fucking mess is beyond anything we’ve ever seen or heard of before. The Bureau was prepared... just not for this.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.05]This fucking mess is beyond anything we’ve ever seen or heard of before. [4.57-6.1]The Bureau was prepared... [6.67-7.8]just not for this.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERGARCIA_57480
lines.text: Rogers said he bumped into someone dressed in old FBC gear. Old old, like from the original manuals.
lines.subtitle: [0.51-4.78]Rogers said he bumped into someone dressed in old FBC gear. [5.24-7.98]Old old, like from the original manuals.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERPHAM_57481
lines.text: Are we running out of uniforms?
lines.subtitle: Are we running out of uniforms?

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERGARCIA_57482
lines.text: The guy apparently said he was “late for everything” and hurried off.
lines.subtitle: The guy apparently said he was “late for everything” and hurried off.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERPHAM_57483
lines.text: Huh. Interesting. Fishy.
lines.subtitle: [0.62-4.61]Huh. Interesting. Fishy.

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERGARCIA_57484
lines.text: Are you thinking - a mole?
lines.subtitle: Are you thinking - a mole?

lines.speaker: LWMAPRANGERPHAM_57485
lines.text: Maybe.
lines.subtitle: Maybe.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57316
lines.text: So, now we know what’s occurring at the Evac Site. A heretofore unseen concentration of the Hiss. It’s... formidable. Worrying.
lines.subtitle: [0.71-3.77]So, now we know what’s occurring at the Evac Site. [4.46-7.18]A heretofore unseen concentration of the Hiss. [8.26-10.99]It’s... formidable. Worrying.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57317
lines.text: Is it a part of the Hiss’s ongoing evolution... or a phenomenon of its own, a centralized energy spike of sorts, feeding itself?
lines.subtitle: [0-3.28]Is it a part of the Hiss’s ongoing evolution... [3.85-9.99]or a phenomenon of its own, a centralized energy spike of sorts, feeding itself?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57318
lines.text: It does have many characteristics of a self-amplifying system. I can only assume the concentration will either continue to escalate until it reaches a culmination point or, conversely, that it eventually runs out of energy and burns out.
lines.subtitle: [0.79-4.02]It does have many characteristics of a self-amplifying system. [5.02-14.56]I can only assume the concentration will either continue to escalate until it reaches a culmination point or, conversely, that it eventually runs out of energy and burns out.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57319
lines.text: I guess we’ll see.
lines.subtitle: I guess we’ll see.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57325
lines.text: A shame about Clarke and Ryder. I believe they were decent people. Hard-working. But... I suppose they knew the risks.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.49]A shame about Clarke and Ryder. [3.82-5.43]I believe they were decent people. [6.48-11.74]Hard-working. But... I suppose they knew the risks.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57326
lines.text: Yes, yes, but I think we’re missing viable opportunities with the use of ley lines. If we can charge the city’s power grid with paranatural energy by aligning with them, there’s bound to be potential for much more.
lines.subtitle: [0.63-5.61]Yes, yes, but I think we’re missing viable opportunities with the use of ley lines. [6.15-10.7]If we can charge the city’s power grid with paranatural energy by aligning with them, [11.25-13.45]there’s bound to be potential for much more.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57327
lines.text: Uh-huh. Well.. our predecessors have researched that to the best of their ability back in the day. So we have a starting point for further study, if needed.
lines.subtitle: [0-6.71]Uh-huh. Well.. our predecessors have researched that to the best of their ability back in the day. [7.77-10.29]So we have a starting point for further study, if needed.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57328
lines.text: Absolutely. It wouldn’t do to overlook the efforts of those who came before us! Speaking of, you were saying something about people?
lines.subtitle: [0-4.47]Absolutely. It wouldn’t do to overlook the efforts of those who came before us! [7.06-10.48]Speaking of, you were saying something about people?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57329
lines.text: Never mind.
lines.subtitle: Never mind.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57330
lines.text: The crew noted some interesting findings down in the subway tunnels. Apparently, the Mold is now interacting favorably with electricity.
lines.subtitle: [0.6-3.75]The crew noted some interesting findings down in the subway tunnels. [4.52-7.75]Apparently, the Mold is now interacting favorably with electricity.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57331
lines.text: Drawn to power, eh? Maybe this is both symbolic and literal. The Mold does seem to be in a state of exponential growth - I wouldn’t be surprised to learn it’s experimenting, trying to find new stimulants, gain more fertile ground, as it were.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.73]Drawn to power, eh? [2.51-4.9]Maybe this is both symbolic and literal. [5.55-8.82]The Mold does seem to be in a state of exponential growth - [9.55-14.45]I wouldn’t be surprised to learn it’s experimenting, trying to find new stimulants, [14.87-16.95]gain more fertile ground, as it were.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57332
lines.text: Sounds like you’re saying the Mold is on steroids?
lines.subtitle: [0.56-3.35]Sounds like you’re saying the Mold is on steroids?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57333
lines.text: In a manner of speaking. Now, I wouldn’t ascribe actual intelligence to it, but... You have to wonder...
lines.subtitle: [0-1.46]In a manner of speaking. [1.47-4.42]Now, I wouldn’t ascribe actual intelligence to it, but... [5.2-6.48]You have to wonder...

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57334
lines.text: So the Patterning is reaching downward, underground. What do we make of that?
lines.subtitle: So the Patterning is reaching downward, underground. What do we make of that?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57335
lines.text: Assuming it’s simply not filling up all available space... um, could the subterranean environment be more beneficial for it somehow? Enclosed.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.34]Assuming it’s simply not filling up all available space... [3.44-9.24]um, could the subterranean environment be more beneficial for it somehow? Enclosed.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57336
lines.text: Unexposed to open air. Closer to groundwater?
lines.subtitle: [0.57-2.97]Unexposed to open air. [3.55-4.85]Closer to groundwater?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57337
lines.text: Closer to continental drift energies?
lines.subtitle: Closer to continental drift energies?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57338
lines.text: Ooh, that’s interesting.
lines.subtitle: Ooh, that’s interesting.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57339
lines.text: Could the Sinkhole be just the first of many? Is the Patterning aiming to create more of them?
lines.subtitle: [0-3.25]Could the Sinkhole be just the first of many? [3.87-6.18]Is the Patterning aiming to create more of them?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57340
lines.text: As in... a network? A means of getting around faster? Or aiming to amplify through interconnectedness?
lines.subtitle: [0.57-1.78]As in... a network? [2.26-4.27]A means of getting around faster? [4.48-7.59]Or aiming to amplify through interconnectedness?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57341
lines.text: Building from the ground up?
lines.subtitle: Building from the ground up?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57342
lines.text: Or the other way around, rather. Hmm.
lines.subtitle: [0.76-4.02]Or the other way around, rather. Hmm.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57343
lines.text: We should’ve seen this coming. How could they be so careless? The CFD was not ready!
lines.subtitle: [0-1.44]We should’ve seen this coming. [2.23-4.19]How could they be so careless? [4.71-6.27]The CFD was not ready!

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57344
lines.text: What else could they do? It was either that or the Hiss destroying us all.
lines.subtitle: [0.58-4.54]What else could they do? It was either that or the Hiss destroying us all.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57345
lines.text: We very nearly were destroyed! This isn’t an arms race - this is supposed to be a measured response to an AWE. Not an opportunity to come up with the most reckless paranatural weaponry imaginable. It’s...
lines.subtitle: [0-2.27]We very nearly were destroyed! [2.98-8.77]This isn’t an arms race - this is supposed to be a measured response to an AWE. [8.87-13.8]Not an opportunity to come up with the most reckless paranatural weaponry imaginable. It’s...

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57346
lines.text: You’re right about the CFD. What’s done is done.
lines.subtitle: [0.7-2.53]You’re right about the CFD. [2.63-4.17]What’s done is done.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57347
lines.text: I guess you were right about the Hiss. They reached a culmination point. Though being proven right on a theory is not as important as preventing catastrophe.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.98]I guess you were right about the Hiss. [2.72-4.33]They reached a culmination point. [5.12-9.06]Though being proven right on a theory is not as important as preventing catastrophe.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57348
lines.text: Well...
lines.subtitle: Well...

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57349
lines.text: We should consider the likely consequences of the CFD... event.
lines.subtitle: [0.77-5.12]We should consider the likely consequences of the CFD... event.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57350
lines.text: We can’t possibly know what is “likely” in a situation as unprecedented as this.
lines.subtitle: [0.54-4.65]We can’t possibly know what is “likely” in a situation as unprecedented as this.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57351
lines.text: True. How about “possible”? “Fathomable”?
lines.subtitle: [0.84-4.96]True. How about “possible”? “Fathomable”?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57352
lines.text: Better. Anyway, I think the consequences will reveal themselves to us, whether we like it or not.
lines.subtitle: [0-6.29]Better. Anyway, I think the consequences will reveal themselves to us, whether we like it or not.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57353
lines.text: Aren’t we fatalistic.
lines.subtitle: [0.72-2.51]Aren’t we fatalistic.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57354
lines.text: Another tragedy resulting in fascinating data! Terrible about the crew, of course - but this spacetime anomaly is unlike any I’ve seen before!
lines.subtitle: [0.57-3.1]Another tragedy resulting in fascinating data! [3.66-9.06]Terrible about the crew, of course - but this spacetime anomaly is unlike any I’ve seen before!

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57355
lines.text: Is the fact that it took place underground relevant, do you think?
lines.subtitle: [0-3.12]Is the fact that it took place underground relevant, do you think?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57356
lines.text: Could be, could be. There are so many fantastic avenues to go down! For instance, the different consciousnesses that exist in all of the temporal variations simultaneously... they are able to observe themselves, but are they a part of a greater whole, or wholly independent manifestations of the self?
lines.subtitle: [0.63-2]Could be, could be. [2.1-4.88]There are so many fantastic avenues to go down! [5.41-11.17]For instance, the different consciousnesses that exist in all of the temporal variations simultaneously... [11.57-16.48]they are able to observe themselves, but are they a part of a greater whole, [16.58-19.69]or wholly independent manifestations of the self?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57357
lines.text: Huh. Beats me.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.75]Huh. Beats me.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57358
lines.text: What feels crucial to me about the Underpass excursion is this: could there have been a way out of the spacetime anomaly the research team was stuck in?
lines.subtitle: [0-3.19]What feels crucial to me about the Underpass excursion is this: [4.14-7.77]could there have been a way out of the spacetime anomaly the research team was stuck in?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57359
lines.text: Or were they just caught in a pre-determined chain of events the moment they stepped foot in the affected area?
lines.subtitle: [0.58-5.97]Or were they just caught in a pre-determined chain of events the moment they stepped foot in the affected area?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57360
lines.text: I think the latter is a more merciful concept.
lines.subtitle: I think the latter is a more merciful concept.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57361
lines.text: Remember; we’re in search of the truth, not comfort.
lines.subtitle: [0.61-3.89]Remember; we’re in search of the truth, not comfort.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57362
lines.text: Temporal paradoxes such as the Underpass anomaly are concerning, I have to admit. If the Patterning is the cause, and if its influence is not only restricted to matter and space - and interestingly, gravity - but also time... We’re looking at a much vaster issue than we originally conceived.
lines.subtitle: [0.67-5.15]Temporal paradoxes such as the Underpass anomaly are concerning, I have to admit. [5.78-10.77]If the Patterning is the cause, and if its influence is not only restricted to matter and space - [10.87-13.54]and interestingly, gravity - but also time... [14.35-17.68]We’re looking at a much vaster issue than we originally conceived.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57363
lines.text: That is to say, we’re screwed.
lines.subtitle: That is to say, we’re screwed.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57364
lines.text: Your words, not mine.
lines.subtitle: Your words, not mine.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57365
lines.text: It’s so obvious now! Of course it’s a Hedron. Of course! Haha!
lines.subtitle: [0-1.94]It’s so obvious now! [2.39-3.91]Of course it’s a Hedron. [4.45-5.67]Of course! Haha!

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57366
lines.text: Yes, obviously the Patterning frequency is a Hedron resonance. It counteracts the Hiss... and reshapes the world.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.22]Yes, obviously the Patterning frequency is a Hedron resonance. [4.91-6.31]It counteracts the Hiss... [7.25-8.8]and reshapes the world.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57367
lines.text: How long has it been on the approach? How could we not tell? Did it cloak its presence? Why would it? It can’t possibly be afraid of us. We’re nothing to it. Less than nothing.
lines.subtitle: [0.67-4.17]How long has it been on the approach? How could we not tell? [4.65-5.99]Did it cloak its presence? [6.29-7.29]Why would it? [7.5-9.49]It can’t possibly be afraid of us. [9.86-10.86]We’re nothing to it. [11.23-12.54]Less than nothing.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57368
lines.text: Yes. It’s not afraid. But maybe... hindered? And yet determined. And powerful.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.63]Yes. It’s not afraid. [1.86-4.23]But maybe... hindered? [5.26-8.39]And yet determined. And powerful.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57369
lines.text: The links the Hedron is trying to form with the Earth - what is their purpose? Their mechanism? A funnel of energy, boosting it? Or just a tether, tying the Hedron to our dimension?
lines.subtitle: [0-1.8]The links the Hedron is trying to form with the Earth - what is their purpose? [1.8-3.27]Their mechanism? A funnel of energy, boosting it? [3.27-5.45]Or just a tether, tying the Hedron to our dimension?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57370
lines.text: Either way, it’s a tactical weak point.
lines.subtitle: Either way, it’s a tactical weak point.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57371
lines.text: So it’s... an interdimensional tug of war? I was never much into sports.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.93]So it’s... an interdimensional tug of war? [5.05-6.76]I was never much into sports.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57372
lines.text: Why did the link form here? It’s hardly coincidental.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.5]Why did the link form here? [3.27-4.83]It’s hardly coincidental.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57373
lines.text: The Oldest House is a Place of Power. A nexus point of ley lines and paranatural energies. And it has housed a Hedron in the past. Is it any wonder this one would be drawn to it?
lines.subtitle: [0-2.54]The Oldest House is a Place of Power. [3.51-6.9]A nexus point of ley lines and paranatural energies. [7.49-9.73]And it has housed a Hedron in the past. [10.81-12.77]Is it any wonder this one would be drawn to it?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57374
lines.text: Do you think the House will hold?
lines.subtitle: Do you think the House will hold?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57375
lines.text: The Oldest House has stood here for eons, in one form or another. I’m sure it’ll survive. Survive us, too.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.42]The Oldest House has stood here for eons, in one form or another. [4.34-5.76]I’m sure it’ll survive. [6.6-7.64]Survive us, too.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57403
lines.text: I hear a tricky old FBC protocol was activated in the Underpass. I didn’t think load-bearing light bulbs were a thing.
lines.subtitle: [0.84-4.57]I hear a tricky old FBC protocol was activated in the Underpass. [5.47-7.86]I didn’t think load-bearing light bulbs were a thing.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57404
lines.text: I wouldn’t put it past the Oldest House. Regardless, the Bureau should have established an automated update system to this protocol. Or at least kept better track of its schedule.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.93]I wouldn’t put it past the Oldest House. [2.88-7.24]Regardless, the Bureau should have established an automated update system to this protocol. [7.92-10.09]Or at least kept better track of its schedule.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57405
lines.text: Given that apparently the structural integrity of the entire building was -- or is -- depending on it... yes. Something a little off about this one.
lines.subtitle: [0-5.07]Given that apparently the structural integrity of the entire building was -- or is -- [5.17-6.17]depending on it... [6.67-9.78]yes. Something a little off about this one.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57406
lines.text: I concur.
lines.subtitle: I concur.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57407
lines.text: The Camera is another interesting Altered Item. Langston must be thrilled.
lines.subtitle: [0.54-3.34]The Camera is another interesting Altered Item. [3.86-5.17]Langston must be thrilled.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57408
lines.text: The folks captured by it were less than thrilled, I hear.
lines.subtitle: [0.78-3.66]The folks captured by it were less than thrilled, I hear.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57409
lines.text: It has a very localized effect. Do we know yet if the “freezing” remains in effect indefinitely if not disrupted? Or does it expire after a time?
lines.subtitle: [0.67-2.68]It has a very localized effect. [3.15-7.39]Do we know yet if the “freezing” remains in effect indefinitely if not disrupted? [7.57-9.49]Or does it expire after a time?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57410
lines.text: That would require active testing.
lines.subtitle: [0.7-2.41]That would require active testing.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57411
lines.text: Hmm. That’ll have to wait.
lines.subtitle: [0.6-2.89]Hmm. That’ll have to wait.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57398
lines.text: Fra Mauro’s influence on people seemed to be strangely benevolent while wholly intrusive.
lines.subtitle: [0.8-5.77]Fra Mauro’s influence on people seemed to be strangely benevolent while wholly intrusive.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57399
lines.text: I would prefer to not be brainwashed myself.
lines.subtitle: [0.55-2.91]I would prefer to not be brainwashed myself.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57400
lines.text: This entity’s influence worked nearly instantly through proximity. But it was reversible. Some functional similarities to being affected by a noxious gas.
lines.subtitle: [1.14-4.83]This entity’s influence worked nearly instantly through proximity. [5.31-10.26]But it was reversible. Some functional similarities to being affected by a noxious gas.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57401
lines.text: Are you now saying Fra’s sphere of influence works on an olfactory principle?
lines.subtitle: [0.92-5.53]Are you now saying Fra’s sphere of influence works on an olfactory principle?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57402
lines.text: Well, not quite that. That would be too silly.
lines.subtitle: [1-3.58]Well, not quite that. [4.81-6.11]That would be too silly.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57394
lines.text: What do you make of this Fra Mauro fellow? Are we pleased with how we dealt with him? Is he?
lines.subtitle: [0.85-3.06]What do you make of this Fra Mauro fellow? [3.42-7.21]Are we pleased with how we dealt with him? Is he?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57395
lines.text: We should prepare for the eventuality that he finds his way out of containment again.
lines.subtitle: [0.87-4.68]We should prepare for the eventuality that he finds his way out of containment again.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57396
lines.text: Hmm. I doubt we have the bandwidth for it now, but after this AWE has been dealt with, we should develop more robust containment procedures.
lines.subtitle: [0.83-7.27]Hmm. I doubt we have the bandwidth for it now, but after this AWE has been dealt with, [7.37-10.04]we should develop more robust containment procedures.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57397
lines.text: Yes. We can’t assume our current containment methods are sufficient. This AWE is proof of that.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57389
lines.text: I wonder... could we draw any parallels between the Speaker Items and the Karaoke Machine? They have some basic similarities.
lines.subtitle: [0.74-6.2]I wonder... could we draw any parallels between the Speaker Items and the Karaoke Machine? [6.96-8.68]They have some basic similarities.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57390

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57391
lines.text: Yes, and while their effects differ, they could be grouped in the same subcategory of Altered Items. Of course, interaction with them does produce vastly different consequences...

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57392
lines.text: I think that would be the correct categorizing method. We can cross-reference, too, of course.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57393
lines.text: Of course.
lines.subtitle: Of course.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57387
lines.text: We of course have seen people be host bodies to a number of entities before, too. But these speakers are interesting in that the speaker item seemed to both possess a host body and subsume a human consciousness.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.27]We of course have seen people be host bodies to a number of entities before, too. [4.87-11.74]But these speakers are interesting in that the speaker item seemed to both possess a host body and subsume a human consciousness.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57388
lines.text: Yes, very flexible of it. And not very common, you’re right. Perhaps due to the Item being a set, with different individual items of the set having subtly different directives that, all told, benefit the whole. A good observation!

[15.35-16.49]A good observation!

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57376
lines.text: Apparently Padmore and Leckie overheard Langston talking to himself about his, uhm, pet. According to him, quite the Hiss-killer.
lines.subtitle: [0-5.56]Apparently Padmore and Leckie overheard Langston talking to himself about his, uhm, pet. [6.62-8.47]According to him, quite the Hiss-killer.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57377
lines.text: Those two say a lot of things.
lines.subtitle: Those two say a lot of things.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57378
lines.text: But if it’s true -- what are we thinking, a paranatural entity? Or... possessed by one?
lines.subtitle: [0-4.82]But if it’s true -- what are we thinking, a paranatural entity? [5.15-6.84]Or... possessed by one?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57379
lines.text: I guess. Could be a third kind altogether. Camouflaging itself as a harmless domesticated animal?
lines.subtitle: [0.53-3.8]I guess. Could be a third kind altogether. [4.56-7.29]Camouflaging itself as a harmless domesticated animal?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTCALDWELL_57380
lines.text: Whatever it is, it seems quite attached to Langston. And Langston to it. Like they’re in a state of equilibrium.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMARKSON_57320
lines.text: What do you make of the Resonant Entity? Quite the combination of both known and unknown factors, resulting in a, in a...

lines.text: A horrific abomination?

lines.text: I suppose that is the strictly human point of view. But in terms of physics, what an exciting prospect - possibly a power transfer process caused by the Patterning colliding with an element vibrating on the same frequency...

lines.speaker: LWOHRANGERCONNOR_57495
lines.text: So, you being a scientist, you’d know how the Hiss works, right? And if... people who were possessed by them can... be cured?
lines.subtitle: [1.11-8.45]So, you being a scientist, you’d know how the Hiss works, right? [9.38-16.38]And if... people who were possessed by them can... be cured?

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMILLER_57496
lines.text: Oh, that’s something we gave up on long ago. At first, we had hopes of discovering a way to reverse the damage, but it couldn’t be done. There was nothing left to save.
lines.subtitle: [0.81-3.66]Oh, that’s something we gave up on long ago. [4.15-9.02]At first, we had hopes of discovering a way to reverse the damage, but it couldn’t be done. [9.12-10.74]There was nothing left to save.

lines.speaker: LWOHRANGERCONNOR_57497

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMILLER_57498
lines.text: The Fadens are... special. Outliers. And the Director didn’t exactly save Dylan. She all but fried his brain, burning the Hiss out. He spent the lockdown in a coma. Anybody else would just die on the spot. I think she tried it once.
lines.subtitle: [0.75-7.3]The Fadens are... special. Outliers. And the Director didn’t exactly save Dylan. [7.48-9.8]She all but fried his brain, burning the Hiss out. lines.speaker: LWOHRANGERCONNOR_57499
lines.text: You know, I... Before the Lockdown failed, I... lost someone close to me.
lines.subtitle: [1.35-8.71]You know, I... Before the Lockdown failed, I... [10.09-12.35]lost someone close to me.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMILLER_57500
lines.text: Oh, I’m sorry to hear that.
lines.subtitle: [0.74-2.92]Oh, I’m sorry to hear that.

lines.speaker: LWOHRANGERCONNOR_57501
lines.text: He... I saw him, afterwards. Deeper inside the building. I didn’t do anything.
lines.subtitle: [0.56-5.7]He... I saw him, afterwards. [6.58-10.09]Deeper inside the building. I didn’t do anything.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMILLER_57502
lines.text: What do you mean “do anything”?

lines.speaker: LWOHRANGERCONNOR_57503
lines.text: I didn’t shoot him. I couldn’t.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.98]I didn’t shoot him. I couldn’t.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMILLER_57504
lines.text: Oh, Cornelia. That’s why you were asking about the Hiss? You think... he can still be saved?
lines.subtitle: [0.72-4.37]Oh, Cornelia. That’s why you were asking about the Hiss? [4.58-7.42]You think... he can still be saved?

lines.speaker: LWOHRANGERCONNOR_57505
lines.text: I have to try. There has to be a way.
lines.subtitle: [0.61-1.99]I have to try. [2.5-4.05]There has to be a way.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMILLER_57506
lines.text: Cornelia, I’m sorry to say this, but... there’s really no way to get your friend back.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.24]Cornelia, I’m sorry to say this, but... [5.52-8.12]there’s really no way to get your friend back.

lines.speaker: LWOHRANGERCONNOR_57507
lines.text: You don’t know that! Not really. We haven’t tried everything, you said it yourself.
lines.subtitle: [1.08-2.41]You don’t know that! [2.83-7.5]Not really. We haven’t tried everything, you said it yourself.

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMILLER_57508
lines.text: That’s not what--
lines.subtitle: That’s not what--

lines.speaker: LWOHSCIENTISTMILLER_57509
lines.text: I know it’s tough. But you have to let him go.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.05]I know it’s tough. [2.93-4.4]But you have to let him go.

lines.speaker: LWOHRANGERCONNOR_57510

lines.subtitle: [0.52-1.72]I know I’m being...

lines.subtitle: [1.53-4.26]I know there’s no hope for him. [6.43-11]My boyfriend. I’m not delusional.

lines.subtitle: I know.

lines.text: It’s just fucking hard.
lines.subtitle: [0.65-4.4]It’s just fucking hard.

lines.speaker: LWOHRANGERCONNOR_57521

lines.text: How far do you think the supplies will last?
lines.subtitle: [0.64-3.09]How far do you think the supplies will last?
