lines.subtitle: [0-2.29]So... it’s all over, huh? [3.06-6.77]I mean, yeah, there’s some loose ends to tie up, but we basically won. [7.41-10.28]I don’t see why we have to still stand here. [10.84-12.69]They should let us go off-duty, take it easy.

lines.speaker: LWFOWRANGERWIECZOREK_58162
lines.text: “And this same flower that smiled today, tomorrow will be dying.”
lines.subtitle: “And this same flower that smiled today, tomorrow will be dying.”

lines.speaker: LWFOWRANGERGLANFORTI_58164
lines.text: ...I never understand a single fucking thing you say.
lines.subtitle: ...I never understand a single fucking thing you say.

lines.speaker: LWFOWRANGERWIECZOREK_58163
lines.text: “People will do anything, no matter how absurd, to avoid facing their own souls.”
lines.subtitle: “People will do anything, no matter how absurd, to avoid facing their own souls.”

lines.speaker: LWFOWRANGERWIECZOREK_58153
lines.text: “There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.”
lines.subtitle: “There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.”

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICOAKLEY_58133
lines.text: I didn’t think we’d ever actually have to do this, you know? The worst case scenario containment stuff. I always thought it was ridiculous.
lines.subtitle: [0.61-2.77]I didn’t think we’d ever actually have to do this, you know? [3.51-5.33]The worst case scenario containment stuff. [6.22-8.32]I always thought it was ridiculous.

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICCLUSKY_58134
lines.text: Not me. I always knew this could happen. And now that it did, we were ready.
lines.subtitle: [0.77-3.23]Not me. I always knew this could happen. [3.58-5.39]And now that it did, we were ready.

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICOAKLEY_58135
lines.text: Pretty lucky.
lines.subtitle: Pretty lucky.

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICCLUSKY_58136
lines.text: Lucky, my ass. Those trucks were already loaded up with the Black Rock and the scaffolding and the tools and whatever the fuck. They were gassed up and ready to go. When they gave the order, the first truck was out the goddamn door five minutes later, and that driver knew exactly where to go. Fuck luck, that’s planning and preparation and hard work.
lines.subtitle: [0.57-2.49]Lucky, my ass. [2.86-8.39]Those trucks were already loaded up with the Black Rock and the scaffolding and the tools and whatever the fuck. [8.49-10.8]They were gassed up and ready to go. [10.99-15.17]When they gave the order, the first truck was out the goddamn door five minutes later, [15.17-17.45]and that driver knew exactly where to go. [17.56-22.51]Fuck luck, that’s planning and preparation and hard work.

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICCLUSKY_58137
lines.text: Makes me proud, man.
lines.subtitle: Makes me proud, man.

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICOAKLEY_58138
lines.text: So... what do you think? Are we good?
lines.subtitle: [0.55-3.22]So... what do you think? [4.04-5.04]Are we good?

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICCLUSKY_58139
lines.text: You tell me. The walls are holding, the zones are doing their job...
lines.subtitle: [0-1.3]You tell me. [1.99-4.62]The walls are holding, the zones are doing their job...

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICOAKLEY_58140
lines.text: So far.
lines.subtitle: So far.

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICCLUSKY_58141
lines.text: You getting pessimistic on me?
lines.subtitle: You getting pessimistic on me?

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICOAKLEY_58142
lines.text: Hell, I don’t know. Just waiting for the other shoe to drop.
lines.subtitle: [0.63-2]Hell, I don’t know. [2.53-4.84]Just waiting for the other shoe to drop.

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICCLUSKY_58143
lines.text: You and me both, pal.
lines.subtitle: You and me both, pal.

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICOAKLEY_58144
lines.text: You’re being quiet.
lines.subtitle: You’re being quiet.

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICCLUSKY_58145
lines.text: Just thinking about logistics. Which walls to take down first, how to stagger the work...
lines.subtitle: [0-1.73]Just thinking about logistics. [1.76-4.19]Which walls to take down first, how to stagger the work...

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICOAKLEY_58146
lines.text: We’re taking them down?
lines.subtitle: We’re taking them down?

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICCLUSKY_58147
lines.text: Well, not yet we’re not, obviously. But eventually we’ll be in the clean-up stage, right? So sooner or later we gotta pack up our toys and haul ‘em back home. Sweep it all under the carpet.
lines.subtitle: [0-5.65]Well, not yet we’re not, obviously. But eventually we’ll be in the clean-up stage, right? [5.75-11.13]So sooner or later we gotta pack up our toys and haul ‘em back home. Sweep it all under the carpet.

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICOAKLEY_58148
lines.text: There’s no way.
lines.subtitle: There’s no way.

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICCLUSKY_58149
lines.text: Never say never.
lines.subtitle: Never say never.

lines.speaker: LWFOWMECHANICOAKLEY_58150
lines.text: I didn’t.
lines.subtitle: I didn’t.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERRYDER_58165
lines.text: So... retirement, huh?
lines.subtitle: So... retirement, huh?

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERSHECTER_58166
lines.text: Seems a little unlikely right now. But assuming we make it through this...
lines.subtitle: [0.64-2.85]Seems a little unlikely right now. [2.95-6.74]But assuming we make it through this...

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERRYDER_58167
lines.text: Well, you earned it. You’re already seven years late because of the lockdown...
lines.subtitle: [0-2.61]Well, you earned it. [3.47-6.48]You’re already seven years late because of the lockdown...

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERSHECTER_58168
lines.text: Yep.
lines.subtitle: Yep.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERRYDER_58169
lines.text: Gonna be weird without you.
lines.subtitle: Gonna be weird without you.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERRYDER_58170
lines.text: Bet you’re eager to get back to the family. They’re still in San Diego, right?
lines.subtitle: [0.53-2.46]Bet you’re eager to get back to the family. [3.05-4.66]They’re still in San Diego, right?

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERSHECTER_58171
lines.text: Last I heard, ‘less they moved... but I’ll find ‘em. The twins’ll be getting pretty big now. Still got some childhood left to spend with me, though...
lines.subtitle: [0.8-4.79]Last I heard, ‘less they moved... but I’ll find ‘em. [5.97-7.78]The twins’ll be getting pretty big now. [8.57-11.23]Still got some childhood left to spend with me, though...

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERRYDER_58172
lines.text: Yeah. They’d like that.
lines.subtitle: Yeah. They’d like that.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERSHECTER_58173
lines.text: I worry about that. They probably think I’m dead.
lines.subtitle: [0.66-1.9]I worry about that. [2.57-4.38]They probably think I’m dead.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERRYDER_58174
lines.text: So that’ll make it a happy surprise. C’mon, grampa. It’ll be good.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.03]So that’ll make it a happy surprise. [3.51-6.4]C’mon, grampa. It’ll be good.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERRYDER_58175
lines.text: So... when you get to see those grandkids, what’re you gonna do?
lines.subtitle: So... when you get to see those grandkids, what’re you gonna do?

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERSHECTER_58176
lines.text: I don’t have the details worked out. Probably spoil ‘em rotten.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.64]I don’t have the details worked out. [4.71-6.16]Probably spoil ‘em rotten.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERRYDER_58177
lines.text: Your daughter’ll appreciate that.
lines.subtitle: [0.54-2.73]Your daughter’ll appreciate that.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERSHECTER_58178
lines.text: It’s what my daddy did with her.
lines.subtitle: It’s what my daddy did with her.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERRYDER_58179
lines.text: Ah, the circle of life.
lines.subtitle: Ah, the circle of life.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERSHECTER_58180
lines.text: Yeah.
lines.subtitle: [0.64-1.64]Yeah.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERSHECTER_58181
lines.text: I’m never gonna get out of here, am I? Either one of these bastard things in Manhattan’ll get me, or this turns into just another lockdown and I run outta years.
lines.subtitle: [0.69-2.81]I’m never gonna get out of here, am I? [4.14-7.07]Either one of these bastard things in Manhattan’ll get me, [7.66-11.48]or this turns into just another lockdown and I run outta years.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERRYDER_58182
lines.text: Hey. Don’t talk like that. We’ll get out of here.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.48]Hey. Don’t talk like that. [2.76-4.05]We’ll get out of here.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERSHECTER_58183
lines.text: Don’t blow smoke up an old man’s ass.
lines.subtitle: [0.59-2.97]Don’t blow smoke up an old man’s ass.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERRYDER_58184
lines.text: Hey. I hear what you’re saying. But you’re not dying here.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.42]Hey. I hear what you’re saying. [2.8-4.56]But you’re not dying here.

lines.speaker: LWZFRANGERSHECTER_58185
lines.text: We’ll see.
lines.subtitle: We’ll see.

lines.speaker: LWZFSCIENTISTSOLOMON_58186
lines.text: God, who would’ve thought the CFD would turn out the way it did... It’s probably for the best it was destroyed.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.09]God, who would’ve thought the CFD would turn out the way it did... [5.1-7.39]It’s probably for the best it was destroyed.

lines.speaker: LWZFSCIENTISTO’BRIEN_58187
lines.text: I think you’re letting your fear guide you. The Pattern is a resource just like any other. We can exploit it to our advantage. It’d be foolish to just ignore it.
lines.subtitle: [0.55-2.5]I think you’re letting your fear guide you. [2.73-4.84]The Pattern is a resource just like any other. [5-8.77]We can exploit it to our advantage. It’d be foolish to just ignore it.

lines.speaker: LWZFSCIENTISTSOLOMON_58188
lines.text: I’m sorry, but that attitude is everything wrong with the FBC. We never learn.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.95]I’m sorry, but that attitude is everything wrong with the FBC. [4.37-5.37]We never learn.

lines.speaker: LWZFSCIENTISTO’BRIEN_58189
lines.text: Whatever.
lines.subtitle: Whatever.

lines.speaker: LWZFSCIENTISTO’BRIEN_58190
lines.text: You know... after seeing what the Hedron did to the Oldest House, maybe you’re right... The Pattern is just... too big, too powerful. Too much. We could never hope to control it.
lines.subtitle: [0-5.06]You know... after seeing what the Hedron did to the Oldest House, maybe you’re right... [5.39-11.19]The Pattern is just... too big, too powerful. Too much. We could never hope to control it.

lines.speaker: LWZFSCIENTISTSOLOMON_58191
lines.text: I’m glad you agree... except my position has also changed, and for the exact same reason. I saw the same thing you did, and it’s just... it’s too big for us to destroy. We can’t do it. It’s just beyond us.
lines.subtitle: [0-6.87]I’m glad you agree... except my position has also changed, and for the exact same reason. [7.51-10.02]I saw the same thing you did, and it’s just... [10.88-12.68]it’s too big for us to destroy. [12.97-13.97]We can’t do it. [14.56-15.88]It’s just beyond us.

lines.speaker: LWZFSCIENTISTO’BRIEN_58192
lines.text: What are you saying?
lines.subtitle: What are you saying?

lines.speaker: LWZFSCIENTISTSOLOMON_58193
lines.text: I think we just have to... ride the wave. Grab the tiger by the tail and see where we end up.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.61]I think we just have to... [2.54-3.54]ride the wave. [4.16-6.99]Grab the tiger by the tail and see where we end up.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_12121
lines.text: Hey Zoe, I just got frozen by a camera, along with everything around me -- and then it... I don't know, jumped away.
lines.subtitle: [0-5.59]Hey Zoe, I just got frozen by a camera, along with everything around me -- and then it... [5.69-7.32]I don't know, jumped away.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_12129
lines.text: Found some photos too, taken from around the city. Maybe they're related?
lines.subtitle: [0-2.93]Found some photos too, taken from around the city. [3.59-4.59]Maybe they're related?

lines.speaker: ZOE_49103
lines.text: Frozen like those Hiss you found in the West Incursion Zone?
lines.subtitle: Frozen like those Hiss you found in the West Incursion Zone?

lines.text: Not exactly.
lines.subtitle: Not exactly.

lines.subtitle: [0-3.04]Found a photo, too, taken from somewhere in the city. [4.07-5.06]Maybe they're related?

lines.text: Frozen like... in a block of ice?
lines.subtitle: Frozen like... in a block of ice?

lines.text: Too traumatizing to talk about, huh?
lines.subtitle: Too traumatizing to talk about, huh?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_49116
lines.text: No. I mean I couldn't move. Not even blink. Like I... was in a photograph.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.22]No. I mean I couldn't move. [2.55-5.55]Not even blink. Like I... was in a photograph.

lines.speaker: ZOE_49115
lines.text: You know, you get yourself into a lot of trouble, Dylan.
lines.subtitle: You know, you get yourself into a lot of trouble, Dylan.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_49118
lines.text: Isn't that the job?
lines.subtitle: Isn't that the job?

lines.speaker: ZOE_49117
lines.text: If you're doing it wrong.
lines.subtitle: If you're doing it wrong.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_49119
lines.text: Yes. I was a popsicle a second ago, but now I'm fine and talking to you.
lines.subtitle: Yes. I was a popsicle a second ago, but now I'm fine and talking to you.

lines.speaker: ZOE_49120
lines.text: Okay, have fun catching it. Bye.

lines.subtitle: Engineering log, Underpass Outpost, Mahir Ayad, logistics officer.

lines.speaker: AYAD_63245
lines.text: We’re having some issues with our gear. Grime, dust, evaporated lubricant -- a couple weeks’ worth of wear and tear in just a few days. The environment isn’t that harsh, but there might be something in the climate -- something to keep an eye on. Another weird detail: Mel was gone for a bit, checking out an area beyond staging. When she got back, the time on her watch was way off. Like two hours twenty minutes off. We synchronized when we started on the expedition. And these are the same watches exactly: FBC-issued, BR-coated, field tested. They’re supposed to be quote-unquote infallible. And once they’re set, they can’t be reset by anyone but me. How does a watch suddenly leap forward the length of a whole movie?

lines.subtitle: Research log, Underpass Outpost, Melanie Grist, hypothetical physics.

lines.speaker: GRIST_63243
lines.text: I am increasingly concerned that the Patterning we have observed over these past few days in the Underpass shows a dwindling reaction to standard inhibitors. This includes the Swiss army knife of resonance dampening that is Black Rock. As we edge ever closer to what I believe is a focal point of the Patterning in the area, where it encroaches on the Oldest House, the growing ferocity of the phenomenon is ironically dampening the dampener. Which is... really scary.

lines.speaker: GRIST_63242
lines.text: Field observations at a molecular level suggest the slow restructuring of Black Rock's hyperstable particles. This is especially troubling since our team, like too much of the FBC, relies on Black Rock for protection. I fear my observations are leading to a terrible possibility: that everything is Patterning, including us, at a rate much more consistent and uniform than we have so far observed, making it difficult to perceive that anything is Patterning at all. This would need to include any and all constants of nature, and could extend the parameters outside these constants. Like effects preceding the cause, or human development, maybe: almost like the instructive induction of cells and embryonic development, scaled way up.

lines.speaker: GRIST_63226
lines.text: I am increasingly concerned that the Patterning we have observed over the year here in the Underpass is getting worse. But I can't be sure of this. Tried and true methods produce nothing of value. Creative questions yield no answers. I think even my own senses may be betraying me. I can't see this escalation. But it's there. Just without a point of reference. Like Schrodinger's cat, inside a box, both alive and dead because you can't see in; except I'm the one in the box. I sound crazy. This is crazy. A make-work suicide mission. We're three darts that Schultz is throwing at a board while blindfolded when we can't be sure there's a board to begin with.

lines.speaker: DRSTEINBECK_63228
lines.text: I was expecting to meet with Jürgen forty minutes ago but he’s gone AWOL. This is the second time, and second team member, who’s forgotten an appointment we made in as many days. I’m beginning to worry that the longer we remain at this camp, the more effect it has on our cognitive abilities, notably memory, emotional regulation, and even a regression of object permanence. It’s not just our sessions either. The team, myself included, are having trouble remembering entire conversations we’ve apparently had... or haven’t. Yesterday, Mahir referred multiple times to a fight he swears he had with me over leaving rations out. I’ve never fought with Mahir. Mahir’s my favorite.

lines.speaker: AYAD_63219
lines.text: Ayad, engineering log. The damage to the tower is catastrophic. Don’t know what happened. One minute all tests were green, it’s working like we need, the next, like someone took a bomb to it or something tore it apart. I can’t reverse the damage. The crazy thing is, I’m still reading data coming off of the tower. Transmission bursts when everything’s offline. Nothing constant. But blips. Multiple frequencies overlapping and fading in then out. I can’t track them. I thought, radio echoes... but no. They’re distinct. I think they’re real. Like there’s more than one tower... crazy. It's crazy. But the transmissions keep coming. Can’t read them. Can’t shake the feeling I sent them.

There’s no Pattern in the abyss... right? But I have to fix the tower. I can’t let our work go to waste.

lines.speaker: DRSTEINBECK_63209
lines.text: I saw myself today. Not like Wundt or a Buddhist might. This was nothing like that kind of introspection or self-awareness. It was closer to a mirror. A living reflection. Like a whole other Maria Steinbeck, somehow standing there, the same unfortunate posture, wide-eyed and scared. She looked exactly like I felt. But these weren’t my wide eyes. It wasn’t my fear. Our brain and body were distinct. I could smell her breath. I wonder when we split, when she became she instead of me, and what happened to her after that. All the things that only she experienced. How that made us different people. Looking in my own eyes without knowing quite what was behind them was a strangely freeing experience. If I die, does this me keep living? Death is less scary when it’s not the only death. It feels liberating to share some responsibility.

lines.text: My physicist theorizes it was a physical phenomenon, of course. Something akin to ball lightning. Our biologist says there's a possibility it was actually alive - an interdimensional microbe, maybe.

lines.text: We brought it back to the station. We didn't... exactly follow proper procedures. But we had to act fast. There was no time for paperwork or approvals. I made a call.

lines.speaker: DOCTORKAZMOUSKI_63376
lines.text: Acting Director Pope, this is Dr. Kazmouski, I’m a neurologist, assigned by Dr. Florez to the Director’s case. You wanted an update on her condition. I’m afraid this is more vague than either of us would prefer, but even so, I think you’ll find it interesting.
lines.subtitle: Acting Director Pope, this is Dr. Kazmouski, I’m a neurologist, assigned by Dr. Florez to the Director’s case. You wanted an update on her condition. I’m afraid this is more vague than either of us would prefer, but even so, I think you’ll find it interesting.

lines.speaker: DOCTORKAZMOUSKI_63375
lines.text: I can confirm that although at first glance her state appears identical to Dylan Faden’s seven-year period of inactivity, it isn’t. The two components of consciousness are wakefulness and awareness. In her brother, both were missing. However, in the case of the Director, there are periodic signs of awareness: we’re getting bursts of alpha, beta and gamma waves on the EEG. That is to say, she’s not awake, but she is thinking. And I do mean thinking, rather than dreaming: we’re getting almost no delta waves.

lines.speaker: FBCCONTAINMENTWORKERREAGAN_63414
lines.text: The entity Fra Mauro, apparently also known as “Fred”, is now back in containment. How he gave us the slip remains a mystery. Much like Fra himself.
lines.subtitle: The entity Fra Mauro, apparently also known as “Fred”, is now back in containment. How he gave us the slip remains a mystery. Much like Fra himself.

lines.speaker: FBCCONTAINMENTWORKERREAGAN_63413
lines.text: Out of all the things we’ve contained over the years, he’s my favorite. I’ve always liked to believe he is a fully benevolent being. Even though we’re not supposed to think like that here.
lines.subtitle: Out of all the things we’ve contained over the years, he’s my favorite. I’ve always liked to believe he is a fully benevolent being. Even though we’re not supposed to think like that here.

lines.speaker: FBCCONTAINMENTWORKERREAGAN_63412
lines.text: But now, with this... this Director business he’s suddenly so into. What’s motivating it? Is his reaction to Director Faden’s disappearance an attempt to be helpful... or opportunistic?
lines.subtitle: But now, with this... this Director business he’s suddenly so into. What’s motivating it? Is his reaction to Director Faden’s disappearance an attempt to be helpful... or opportunistic?

lines.speaker: FBCCONTAINMENTWORKERREAGAN_63411
lines.text: It seems unlikely that he just suddenly got power-hungry. Maybe he just got... curious? Wanted to be involved? To feel like part of the team?
lines.subtitle: It seems unlikely that he just suddenly got power-hungry. Maybe he just got... curious? Wanted to be involved? To feel like part of the team?

lines.speaker: FBCCONTAINMENTWORKERREAGAN_63410
lines.text: But if that’s how he acts out of containment, brainwashing people, bending them to his will - that’s hardly benevolent. Unless he’s not doing it on purpose? Maybe it’s just... an effect he has on people? Out of his control?
lines.subtitle: But if that’s how he acts out of containment, brainwashing people, bending them to his will - that’s hardly benevolent. Unless he’s not doing it on purpose? Maybe it’s just... an effect he has on people? Out of his control?

lines.speaker: FBCCONTAINMENTWORKERREAGAN_63409
lines.text: I don’t know. I don’t even know if I actually like him or if I just think I do, if he made me think that way.
lines.subtitle: I don’t know. I don’t even know if I actually like him or if I just think I do, if he made me think that way.

lines.speaker: FBCCONTAINMENTWORKERREAGAN_63408
lines.text: I guess I have to file an incident report, just in case.

lines.text: “FBC” stands for Federal Bureau of Control. We’re a little bit like the FBI or CIA, except we deal with AWEs or “Altered World Events”, like the one that took place in your hometown. Now, our mission is to study, contain, and control paranatural phenomena.

lines.text: You usually you have so much to say. Well, I’m glad you’re listening, because this is important. You told us you think you can control your abilities now, but I heard you don’t want to use them again. I’m afraid that won’t be an option.

lines.text: Five years and all we’ve done is waste our time. Disappointment at every turn. And now, just when we finally make progress, somebody dies. The Bureau cannot weather any further disappointments, Dylan.

lines.text: I call it the Mobile Containment Device. Now, if you lose control of your abilities again, I just press this little button.

lines.text: When you first... When we first brought you in. I saw so... so much potential. The opportunity for you, The Bureau, for scientific advancement. You may not believe this, but I really thought we were going to make your life better. Ridiculous. It's ridiculous.
lines.subtitle: When you first... When we first brought you in. I saw so... so much potential. The opportunity for you, The Bureau, for scientific advancement. You may not believe this, but I really thought we were going to make your life better. Ridiculous. It's ridiculous.

lines.text: I just-- I have to take care of some things first.

lines.text: Roberts was on both of us, in a way. The later incident, though, when so many died. I-- I wanted results at any cost. I went too far and I pushed too hard.

lines.speaker: DRDARLING_68852
lines.text: I did what I had to do to protect the Bureau. This-- this mortal dimension. So, I had to lie to maintain my position.

lines.text: Trench is lost. I’m sure of that now. The situation is--

lines.text: My actions were... unpleasant. Unethical, yes. Necessary.

lines.speaker: JESSE_71882
lines.text:
My name is Jesse Faden. And I am the Director of the Federal Bureau of Control. But that wasn't always the case. When we were kids, my brother Dylan and I found something. A slide projector. We met a presence. A protector. It became a part of us. But things went wrong. Dylan was…gone. I spent years looking for him. Until finally I found my way to a place in New York that doesn't 
exist on any map. The Federal Bureau of Control. A secret government agency dedicated to the 
study, containment, and control of the paranatural. They call this place the Oldest House. A Place of Power. Inside its walls, the laws of physics 
are…more of a suggestion. But something else had gotten there first. A hostile, extradimensional resonance that corrupts everything it touches. The Hiss. The whole building was under lockdown. Nothing could get out. Not yet anyway. The previous Director, Zachariah Trench, was dead. I picked up his gun. The Service Weapon. The Director is chosen by the Board, a strange entity that's as mysterious as it is bossy. I passed their test. They made ME the new Director. Gave me the task of stopping the Hiss. Whatever the fuck that meant But I wasn't alone. Emily Pope, a research expert. Simon Arish. Chief of Security. And Casper Darling. The Bureau's missing Head of Research. Dylan was in there too… Somewhere. The Bureau had treated him like a science project. His abilities made him a Prime Candidate for the role of Director. They called him "P6." When it all went wrong, they locked him away. I fought through the shifting halls of the Oldest House. Each room weirder than the last. And, finally, I found him. But the Hiss had gotten there first. Dylan was one of them. I wasn't letting my brother go. Not again. I had to stop the Hiss at the source. The Slide Projector, the same one we found as kids, was here, in the Oldest House. Trench had used it to open a door into the Hiss dimension. I had to find it and shut it down. In Dimensional Research, I discovered "the Hedron". That same being we'd first encountered as 
kids. The Bureau had used the Slide Projector to capture it. But The Hiss followed me in…and killed the Hedron. I bound the Slide Projector to myself. I cleansed Dylan of the Hiss. But he's been in a coma ever since. I stayed. I'm the Director now.  The Oldest House is still under lockdown. Containing the Hiss in here with us is my 
responsibility. I thought the walls would hold.

lines.text: Hey...
lines.subtitle: Hey...

lines.text: <inhuman noise>
lines.subtitle: <inhuman noise>

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33011
lines.text: Let's get you home.
lines.subtitle: Let's get you home.

lines.speaker: WILSON_33010
lines.text: He's dying! Hurry!
lines.subtitle: He's dying! Hurry!

lines.speaker: RANGERCOX_32837
lines.text: Willllllllsssssss...
lines.subtitle: [0-3.5]Willllllllsssssss...

lines.speaker: RANGERCOX_32851
lines.text: Soooooooooooonnnnnnnn...
lines.subtitle: [0-3.29]Soooooooooooonnnnnnnn...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33019
lines.text: Another expedition team member is dead, Zoe. Wilson was here, but he disappeared.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.3]Another expedition team member is dead, Zoe. [3.05-4.94]Wilson was here, but he disappeared.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33095
lines.text: Said something about going back to the Threshold.
lines.subtitle: Said something about going back to the Threshold.

lines.speaker: ZOE_33018
lines.text: Find him.
lines.subtitle: Find him.

lines.speaker: ZOE_33015
lines.text: Dylan? What's going on?
lines.subtitle: Dylan? What's going on?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33014
lines.text: Something happened. I'll call you back when I figure out what.
lines.subtitle: Something happened. I'll call you back when I figure out what.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33030
lines.text: Zoe? I found Wilson.
lines.subtitle: Zoe? I found Wilson.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33042
lines.text: He's dead.
lines.subtitle: He's dead.

lines.speaker: ZOE_33029
lines.text: Dammit. Whatever killed that team, let's hope it ends here.
lines.subtitle: Dammit. Whatever killed that team, let's hope it ends here.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33035
lines.text: I was wrong, Zoe. I thought Wilson was a murderer, but if someone killed the team, it wasn't him...
lines.subtitle: [0-1.96]I was wrong, Zoe. [2.72-8.15]I thought Wilson was a murderer, but if someone killed the team, it wasn't him...

lines.speaker: ZOE_33036
lines.text: Then let's hope it wasn't murder. You can't win them all, Dylan.
lines.subtitle: Then let's hope it wasn't murder. You can't win them all, Dylan.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33037
lines.text: The FBC was reckless with the Threshold Zoe. No one should have authorized expeditions unless they were sure it was safe. Didn't the Bureau learn anything from the Hiss?
lines.subtitle: [0-2.88]The FBC was reckless with the Threshold Zoe. [3.58-7.14]No one should have authorized expeditions unless they were sure it was safe. [8.03-10.75]Didn't the Bureau learn anything from the Hiss?

lines.speaker: ZOE_33038
lines.text: The Dig Site was discovered before the FBC outside of the lockdown knew anything about the Hiss, Dylan. We'll update our procedures, of course, but--
lines.subtitle: [0-4.95]The Dig Site was discovered before the FBC outside of the lockdown knew anything about the Hiss, Dylan. [6.25-9.48]We'll update our procedures, of course, but--

lines.speaker: ZOE_33041
lines.text: You're right. It shouldn't have happened like this.
lines.subtitle: You're right. It shouldn't have happened like this.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33039
lines.text: I got so close to figuring it out. I was hoping I could save at least one of them...
lines.subtitle: [0-2.31]I got so close to figuring it out. [3.16-5.31]I was hoping I could save at least one of them...

lines.speaker: ZOE_33040
lines.text: You can't save everyone, Dylan.
lines.subtitle: You can't save everyone, Dylan.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33062
lines.text: Agh...!
lines.subtitle: [0-1]Agh...!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33067
lines.text: Wilson says goodbye...
lines.subtitle: Wilson says goodbye...

lines.speaker: ZOE_33076
lines.text: Dylan? I just got word. Wilson's turned himself in. Says his team caught a disease in the Threshold. They're gonna quarantine him in containment until we figure out how to treat it. Once we get resources on it, we'll close off the Dig Site too so no one else gets hurt.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.88]Dylan? I just got word. [2.44-6.28]Wilson's turned himself in. Says his team caught a disease in the Threshold. [6.93-9.68]They're gonna quarantine him in containment until we figure out how to treat it. [10.47-14.61]Once we get resources on it, we'll close off the Dig Site too so no one else gets hurt.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33084
lines.text: I can't let Wilson ruin his life. It's not a disease, Zoe. His team found intelligent life in that Threshold. The situation is secure now, but he was afraid that if the FBC knew the truth, they wouldn't leave the Dig Site alone.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.92]I can't let Wilson ruin his life. [2.6-4.16]It's not a disease, Zoe. [4.74-7.38]His team found intelligent life in that Threshold. [7.93-12.69]The situation is secure now, but he was afraid that if the FBC knew the truth, [13.35-15.05]they wouldn't leave the Dig Site alone.

lines.speaker: ZOE_33086
lines.text: His fears are warranted.
lines.subtitle: His fears are warranted.

lines.speaker: ZOE_33085
lines.text: But you did the right thing by telling me. Probably just saved him from a lifetime of containment. Though I doubt he'll get to keep his job.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.94]But you did the right thing by telling me. [2.83-4.98]Probably just saved him from a lifetime of containment. [5.68-7.88]Though I doubt he'll get to keep his job.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33082
lines.text: Understood. Sorry I couldn't do more to help.
lines.subtitle: Understood. Sorry I couldn't do more to help.

lines.speaker: ZOE_33083
lines.text: Can't solve them all, Dylan. Thanks for trying.
lines.subtitle: Can't solve them all, Dylan. Thanks for trying.

lines.speaker: ZOE_33080
lines.text: At least it's over now.
lines.subtitle: At least it's over now.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_71033
lines.text: Hey Zoe, looks like someone's set up traps for the Hiss and I don't think it's the FBC. Might be worth looking into...
lines.subtitle: [0-4.45]Hey Zoe, looks like someone's set up traps for the Hiss and I don't think it's the FBC. [5.06-6.37]Might be worth looking into...

lines.speaker: ZOE_71032
lines.text: Be my guest. But I have a hard time believing anyone's still alive out there.
lines.subtitle: Be my guest. But I have a hard time believing anyone's still alive out there.

lines.speaker: ZOE_71031
lines.text: Really? We mined a lot of the city, Dylan... But can't hurt to double check.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.81]Really? We mined a lot of the city, Dylan... [3.58-5.96]But can't hurt to double check.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_30475
lines.text: Halt, intruder!
lines.subtitle: [0-0.94]Halt, intruder!

options.text: You're making things harder out here
You have a unique way of speaking

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16264
lines.text: Hello? What is this place--
lines.subtitle: Hello? What is this place--

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16263
lines.text: This is my fortress, my port in the storm. I built it with my very own hands!
lines.subtitle: [0-2.99]This is my fortress, my port in the storm. [3.09-5.68]I built it with my very own hands!

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16265
lines.text: It's a bunker.
lines.subtitle: It's a bunker.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16266
lines.text: O-kay... I'm with the government. We can evacuate you to a safe place.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.04]O-kay... I'm with the government. [3.25-5.21]We can evacuate you to a safe place.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16270
lines.text: One must be ready for anything -- this is what I've been preparing for all my life.
lines.subtitle: One must be ready for anything -- this is what I've been preparing for all my life.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_71030
lines.text: You're making things harder out here for the people trying to help.
lines.subtitle: You're making things harder out here for the people trying to help.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_71029
lines.text: A lot harder...
lines.subtitle: A lot harder...

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16281
lines.text: My meaning is not to harm innocents, though. Just the...
lines.subtitle: My meaning is not to harm innocents, though. Just the...

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16280
lines.text: ...the ones that are coming. It's either me or them!
lines.subtitle: [0-1.59]...the ones that are coming. [2.35-5.05]It's either me or them!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16279
lines.text: Is there anyone in there with you?
lines.subtitle: Is there anyone in there with you?

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16278
lines.text: Only I. Some people came knocking at my door, offering the very thing you're trying to tempt me with.
lines.subtitle: Only I. Some people came knocking at my door, offering the very thing you're trying to tempt me with.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16277
lines.text: I could see them from my surveillance monitors, getting slaughtered by those... unearthly monsters.
lines.subtitle: I could see them from my surveillance monitors, getting slaughtered by those... unearthly monsters.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16276
lines.text: They're not the ones I am waiting for. Or are they?
lines.subtitle: They're not the ones I am waiting for. Or are they?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16283
lines.text: You seem to have a... Unique way of speaking.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.84]You seem to have a... [2.83-4.93]Unique way of speaking.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16284
lines.text: And what of it? Perhaps it is you who has an ordinary, and I dare say, uninspired, way of speaking.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.13]And what of it? [1.67-9.57]Perhaps it is you who has an ordinary, and I dare say, uninspired, way of speaking.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16285
lines.text: Listen, we can move you someplace safe. It'd be nicer than your bunker. More social at least.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.03]Listen, we can move you someplace safe. It'd be nicer than your bunker. [4.78-7.3]More social at least.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16286
lines.text: Pshaw! What fool would believe a man who offers protection against monsters? You can not guarantee anyone's safety.
lines.subtitle: [0-6.72]Pshaw! What fool would believe a man who offers protection against monsters? [7.47-9.55]You can not guarantee anyone's safety.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_29394
lines.text: I'm not abandoning my safe haven. And there's nothing wrong with a few traps!
lines.subtitle: [0-2.53]I'm not abandoning my safe haven. [3.15-5.31]And there's nothing wrong with a few traps!

options.text: You're making things harder out here
You have a unique way of speaking

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16291
lines.text: My word! Your skills are beyond measure!
lines.subtitle: My word! Your skills are beyond measure!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16303
lines.text: See? I can handle the monsters.
lines.subtitle: See? I can handle the monsters.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16300
lines.text: I do see. Interesting! You seem to be an oddity.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.03]I do see. [1.29-4.32]Interesting! You seem to be an oddity.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16297
lines.text: Are you one of the shape people?
lines.subtitle: Are you one of the shape people?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16305
lines.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa. What are "shape people"?
lines.subtitle: Whoa, whoa, whoa. What are "shape people"?

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16304
lines.text: Shh, not so loud! You seem not to be informed of their arrival. Unlike myself. Hence, the fort.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.35]Shh, not so loud! [2.98-4.89]You seem not to be informed of their arrival. [5.79-8.68]Unlike myself. Hence, the fort.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16302
lines.text: I've been called worse than an oddity.
lines.subtitle: I've been called worse than an oddity.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16301
lines.text: So have I. Many a time.
lines.subtitle: [1.03-2.03]So have I. [2.7-3.7]Many a time.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16299
lines.text: I could use a man of your skills. Sadly I have become separated from my dear Granny and Olivia. Will you return them to me?
lines.subtitle: [0-2.7]I could use a man of your skills. [3.64-8.96]Sadly I have become separated from my dear Granny and Olivia. [9.49-11.25]Will you return them to me?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16298
lines.text: Uh, sure, I guess I can do that.
lines.subtitle: Uh, sure, I guess I can do that.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16296
lines.text: Huzzah! You see, when the world began to end, I was at the gym I own when the city was besieged. I was in such a rush to reach my fort that I left them both behind. Granny and Olivia are all I have left in this world.
lines.subtitle: [0-7.78]Huzzah! You see, when the world began to end, I was at the gym I own when the city was besieged. [8.26-13.34]I was in such a rush to reach my fort that I left them both behind. [14.12-19.38]Granny and Olivia are all I have left in this world.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16295
lines.text: Well, there's my brother too but we don't even talk these days.
lines.subtitle: Well, there's my brother too but we don't even talk these days.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16319
lines.text: I thought you wanted solitude.
lines.subtitle: I thought you wanted solitude.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16318
lines.text: Like my wise old Granny used to say: a family does not a man make, a man makes a family. She came from a different time, of course.
lines.subtitle: [0-8.74]Like my wise old Granny used to say: a family does not a man make, a man makes a family. [10.33-11.85]She came from a different time, of course.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16321
lines.text: I can relate. I don't have a lot of family left either. In fact, I've been looking for my sister Jesse she--
lines.subtitle: [0-3]I can relate. I don't have a lot of family left either. [3.25-6.01]In fact, I've been looking for my sister Jesse she--

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16320
lines.text: Do not get distracted by personal drama - you're meant to aid me!
lines.subtitle: Do not get distracted by personal drama - you're meant to aid me!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16317
lines.text: You own a gym?
lines.subtitle: You own a gym?

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16316
lines.text: Yes. I train rigorously; one has to stay fit to survive. Does that surprise you?
lines.subtitle: [0-4.76]Yes. I train rigorously; one has to stay fit to survive. [5.73-6.98]Does that surprise you?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_29427
lines.text: No, you just don't sound... Nevermind.
lines.subtitle: No, you just don't sound... Nevermind.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16315
lines.text: Poor Granny was at home when I had to flee. You'll find the place with ease. It's your people that set up the "evacuation center" right next to it, after all. I've donned my door with a trusty digital lock. The code is 8521.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.73]Poor Granny was at home when I had to flee. [3.6-5.72]You'll find the place with ease. [6.29-12.19]It's your people that set up the "evacuation center" right next to it, after all. [13.09-16.55]I've donned my door with a trusty digital lock. [17.05-20.26]The code is 8521.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16314
lines.text: 8521, got it. And Olivia?
lines.subtitle: 8521, got it. And Olivia?

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16313
lines.text: My sweet Olivia. Like a ray of April sunshine! She's trapped at the gym. You'll find the place on main street -- but last I saw, it was swarming with the monsters.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.52]My sweet Olivia. [4-6.64]Like a ray of April sunshine! [7.41-8.77]She's trapped at the gym. [9.06-14.98]You'll find the place on main street -- but last I saw, it was swarming with the monsters.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16311
lines.text: The gym, gotcha. I'll bring them here and then we can transport you all somewhere safe.
lines.subtitle: The gym, gotcha. I'll bring them here and then we can transport you all somewhere safe.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_29408
lines.text: Only an oddity such as the shape people could handle the monsters like that.
lines.subtitle: [1.72-6.22]Only an oddity such as the shape people could handle the monsters like that.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_29416
lines.text: I need your help reuniting me with dear Granny and my sweet Olivia.
lines.subtitle: I need your help reuniting me with dear Granny and my sweet Olivia.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16326
lines.text: Oh, Granny is... more compact than I expected.
lines.subtitle: Oh, Granny is... more compact than I expected.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16328
lines.text: So you're Olivia. Nice to meet you.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.29]So you're Olivia. [2.19-3.19]Nice to meet you.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16425
lines.text: I'm back with Granny. She isn't quite what I expected.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.03]I'm back with Granny. [1.81-3.82]She isn't quite what I expected.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16421
lines.text: Is she in good spirits?
lines.subtitle: Is she in good spirits?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16427
lines.text: All right, I'm back with Granny. She's uh... quite light.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.68]All right, I'm back with Granny. [3-5.45]She's uh... quite light.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16426
lines.text: She and Olivia will have a lovely time together, I'm sure.
lines.subtitle: [1.33-5.75]She and Olivia will have a lovely time together, I'm sure.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_71026
lines.text: I've got bad news. Your... Your brother...
lines.subtitle: [0-1.67]I've got bad news. [2.68-4.95]Your... Your brother...

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16423
lines.text: You don't have to say it. There's not much chance for anyone out there, is there?
lines.subtitle: [0-1.75]You don't have to say it. [1.93-4.65]There's not much chance for anyone out there, is there?

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16422
lines.text: I just wish... He told me he wanted to go to your "evacuation center". He begged me to come with him, but I chose the bunker. He must not have wanted to go without me. Now I'm here. Alone.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.03]I just wish... [1.9-5.95]He told me he wanted to go to your "evacuation center". [6.27-9.8]He begged me to come with him, but I chose the bunker. [10.4-12.36]He must not have wanted to go without me. [12.99-15.35]Now I'm here. Alone.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16420
lines.text: All right, I found Olivia too. Although, she wasn't what I thought she'd be, either.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.01]All right, I found Olivia too. [2.65-4.95]Although, she wasn't what I thought she'd be, either.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16419
lines.text: She can keep Granny company. Huzzah!
lines.subtitle: She can keep Granny company. Huzzah!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16418
lines.text: I'm back, and I've got both Granny and Olivia with me.
lines.subtitle: I'm back, and I've got both Granny and Olivia with me.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16417
lines.text: What a great relief! Thank you. Now, just carefully leave them there by the door. I'll bring them in when it's nice and safe.
lines.subtitle: [0-2.03]What a great relief! [2.28-7.83]Thank you. Now, just carefully leave them there by the door. [8.63-11.65]I'll bring them in when it's nice and safe.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16428
lines.text: You know what. I have to say, they weren't quite what I expected.
lines.subtitle: [0-1]You know what. [1.64-4.77]I have to say, they weren't quite what I expected.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16429
lines.text: That's the trouble with expectations. One must keep an open mind!
lines.subtitle: [0-2.94]That's the trouble with expectations. [3.47-5.98]One must keep an open mind!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16430
lines.text: I've lost people too. It's not easy, but you have to keep going. That's what they'd want.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.26]I've lost people too. [2.58-6.56]It's not easy, but you have to keep going. [7.17-8.25]That's what they'd want.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16431
lines.text: That's what Granny always said.
lines.subtitle: [0.95-2.99]That's what Granny always said.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16432
lines.text: I'm sorry.
lines.subtitle: I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16433
lines.text: It's not your fault. I'm thankful for your help.
lines.subtitle: [0-1.1]It's not your fault. [1.67-3.17]I'm thankful for your help.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16434
lines.text: You could say that.
lines.subtitle: You could say that.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16435
lines.text: Great, excellent!
lines.subtitle: Great, excellent!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16436
lines.text: When did your Granny die?
lines.subtitle: When did your Granny die?

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16437
lines.text: What a rude thing to insinuate about someone.
lines.subtitle: What a rude thing to insinuate about someone.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16438
lines.text: Oh, I found something. From your brother's place. It's a photo of him at a cabin with someone. Is that you?
lines.subtitle: [0-4.05]Oh, I found something. From your brother's place. [4.59-7.71]It's a photo of him at a cabin with someone. [8.53-9.33]Is that you?

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16439
lines.text: We took that photo on a hiking trip upstate. Getting back to nature really elevates the soul -- I think he felt the same way.
lines.subtitle: [0-4.16]We took that photo on a hiking trip upstate. [5.06-11.35]Getting back to nature really elevates the soul -- I think he felt the same way.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16442
lines.text: You can leave it on the table for me. Thank you.
lines.subtitle: You can leave it on the table for me. Thank you.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16444
lines.text: While I enjoy having Granny and Olivia back, it's not really... enough. Especially with what's going on. The end of times.
lines.subtitle: [0-6.1]While I enjoy having Granny and Olivia back, it's not really... enough. [6.62-10.22]Especially with what's going on. The end of times.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16445
lines.text: My brother and I had our differences, but I do miss his company. Could you go find him? Bring him here?
lines.subtitle: [0-5.44]My brother and I had our differences, but I do miss his company. [6.14-7.48]Could you go find him? [7.96-9.01]Bring him here?

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16452
lines.text: Now, carefully set Granny down there by the door. I'll bring her in when it's nice and safe.
lines.subtitle: [0-3.74]Now, carefully set Granny down there by the door. [4.06-6.31]I'll bring her in when it's nice and safe.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16453
lines.text: But what of my darling Olivia? She's still out there! With those ghoulish monsters and the...
lines.subtitle: [0-2.86]But what of my darling Olivia? [3.23-4.55]She's still out there! [4.7-6.28]With those ghoulish monsters and the...

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16454
lines.text: ...the shapes. Watching. Waiting.
lines.subtitle: ...the shapes. Watching. Waiting.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16455
lines.text: I'll get her too, don't worry.
lines.subtitle: I'll get her too, don't worry.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16457
lines.text: I'm back. And I've got... Olivia.
lines.subtitle: I'm back. And I've got... Olivia.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16458
lines.text: Is she feeling all right?
lines.subtitle: Is she feeling all right?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16459
lines.text: I can't really tell.
lines.subtitle: I can't really tell.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_16460
lines.text: You have eyes, don't you?
lines.subtitle: You have eyes, don't you?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16461
lines.text: You said you two don't get along. Why?
lines.subtitle: You said you two don't get along. Why?

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_29448
lines.text: My brother never took me seriously.
lines.subtitle: My brother never took me seriously.

lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST_29449
lines.text: And he didn't believe that the shape people were going to un-shape Earth so they can re-shape it in their image. But look who had it right all along!
lines.subtitle: [0-6.25]And he didn't believe that the shape people were going to un-shape Earth so they can re-shape it in their image. [7.28-10.43]But look who had it right all along!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_16462
lines.text: Is your brother an actual human being?
lines.subtitle: Is your brother an actual human being?
